post.summary: Re-bind agent to a new API key
post.description:
Updates the agent's key binding to a new provider API key hash. The agent ID, traces, alignment card, integrity score, and trust edges are fully preserved.

**Security model**: Your API key is hashed on your device (SHA-256) before transmission — the raw key is never sent to Mnemom servers.

**Named agents**: If this agent was registered with a name (via `x-mnemom-agent`), hash the new key as `SHA256(newKey + '|' + agentName)` before submitting.

**Conflict**: If the new key was already used and auto-created a new agent, the endpoint returns `409` with the conflicting agent ID.

new_key_hash.description: First 16 hex characters of SHA256(newApiKey) for unnamed agents, or SHA256(newApiKey + '|' + agentName) for named agents. Compute client-side — do not transmit the raw key.

key_prefix.description: First 16 characters of the new provider API key. Stored for display — not sensitive. If provided, returned in the response.

200.description: Agent successfully re-bound to the new key.

post.description: Resurrects a tombstoned agent by clearing `deleted_at` — the counterpart to [POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/tombstone](/api-reference/endpoint/post-agents-agent-id-tombstone). Lets an org owner/admin override a tombstone (e.g. a key agent a dev removed), or a creator undo their own. Authorized for an org owner/admin OR the agent's creator. Returns 409 for agents that went through GDPR erasure (`DELETE`), whose data was permanently cascaded away and cannot be restored.

409.description: Agent was permanently erased (GDPR Art.17) and cannot be restored

post.summary: Re-verify AAP traces against updated card
post.description: Re-runs AAP structural verification of the agent's stored traces against its currently-active alignment card. **Paginated, and a single call is not a full re-verification:** at most 40 traces are processed per call (Cloudflare Workers subrequest limit). Use `has_more` / `next_offset` to walk the remainder — a caller that stops after one page leaves later traces carrying verdicts from the previous card. `complete` is true only when the pass reached the end of the agent's traces with no write errors; the reputation score is recomputed only on such a pass, and `reputation_recompute_skipped_reason` says why it was not.

total_traces.description: Exact total number of traces stored for this agent, or null if the count could not be established. Null means coverage is UNKNOWN — not zero, and not complete.

traces_scanned.description: offset + rows processed in this call.

has_more.description: True if traces beyond this page remain un-re-verified.

next_offset.description: Offset to pass to the next call, or null when there is no next page.

complete.description: True only if this pass reached the end of the agent's traces with no write errors. False means the agent's history is NOT yet fully consistent with the current card.

reputation_recomputed.description: Whether the agent's reputation score was recomputed. Only ever true on a complete pass that updated at least one trace.

post.summary: Re-evaluate AIP checkpoints against updated card
Retro-correct past Protection screening verdicts against the current card
post.description: Re-buckets the agent's past NON-clear Safe House screening decisions (`sh_evaluations`) against the agent's CURRENT composed Protection card thresholds and durably flips any that are no longer violations. Deterministic threshold re-bucketing, not a re-run of the L1/L2 detector models. Mirrors `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/reverify/aip` (tags/checkpoints.ts) structurally (MNE-7172).

changed_clauses.description: Optional list of Protection card clause paths that changed, recorded on the audit trail only.

get.summary: List disagreement reviews for an agent
get.description: Lists review records created when an action was disagreed-with enough to require human adjudication. Filter by `status` (`pending`, `review`, `applied`, `dismissed`). Reviews propose a card amendment that can be accepted or rejected via the apply/dismiss endpoints.

post.description: Applies the review's `proposed_amendment.action` to the agent's active alignment card by appending it to `autonomy_envelope.bounded_actions`. Updates the review status to `applied`. Only reviews in `pending` or `review` status may be applied.

get.description: Returns the per-agent operational observer-rollout flags (observer V2 primary / V1 shadow). MNE-556 P4: the former behavioral toggles (AAP/AIP, proof, nudge strategy, DDR mode, analyze-output) moved to the composed alignment card and are no longer returned here.

put.description: Partial update — include only the fields to change. MNE-556 P4: the former behavioral toggles (aap_enabled, aip_enabled, proof_enabled, proof_rate, nudge_strategy, ddr_mode, analyze_output) were removed; that config is now authored on the composed alignment card (PUT /agents/{id}/alignment-card). Only the observer-rollout flags are accepted here.

observer_v2_primary_enabled.description: Whether the V2 observer retune is authoritative for this agent (default true).

observer_v1_shadow_enabled.description: Whether the V1 observer runs in parallel shadow for this agent (default false).

get.summary: List historical sideband advisories for an agent (legacy)
get.description: Pre-cutover sideband.* rows still present in pending_advisories. Sunsetting after the ADR-048 D+30 cleanup; consume governance_signals instead for forward-going observations.

get.summary: Runtime composite — alignment + protection + capabilities in one call
get.description: Returns the agent's complete operational envelope as a single response: composed alignment card, composed protection card, and a `capabilities[]` array of full tool definitions (from the W1.1 tools registry — `{name, class, domain, description, schema, source_connector, grant_provenance}`, NOT bare name strings). SDK consumers (first-party SDKs, future Tier-1 customers, OSC instances) call this instead of assembling the envelope client-side. ETag-driven 304 short-circuit; `Cache-Control: private, max-age=60`. cards-as-primitive Phase 4 W2.3.

ETag.description: `"sha256:<hex>"` of the combined alignment + protection + capabilities hash.

X-Card-Version.description: `max(alignment.version, protection.version)`.

304.description: Not Modified — the client's `If-None-Match` matches the current combined ETag.

get.summary: Server-Sent Events stream of canonical card changes.
get.description: Returns a `text/event-stream` connection. Each new `card_attestations` row for the agent emits a `card_changed` SSE frame. Per-connection cap of 5 minutes; clients reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` (the log_index of the last seen frame) to resume. cards-as-primitive Phase 5 C1.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: log_index cursor; omit to start at the current head.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: SSE reconnect convention; takes precedence over `since` when both are present.

200.description:
SSE stream (`text/event-stream`). Each frame is `event: card_changed
id: <log_index>
data: {...}

`.

post.description: Soft-deletes an agent: sets `deleted_at` so it disappears from the org fleet/dashboard while KEEPING all data (traces, checkpoints, proofs) for audit. Reversible via [POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/restore](/api-reference/endpoint/post-agents-agent-id-restore). Distinct from `DELETE /v1/agents/{agent_id}`, which is the irreversible GDPR Art.17 erasure cascade. Authorized for an org owner/admin of the agent's org OR the agent's own creator. Idempotent: tombstoning an already-tombstoned agent returns 200.

get.summary: Get traces for agent (AAP query alias)
List trust edges from or to an agent
get.description: Returns trust-relationship edges that the agent participates in. `direction=outbound` returns edges originating from this agent; `inbound` returns edges pointing at this agent; `both` (default) deduplicates.

post.summary: Create a trust edge from this agent to another
post.description: Caller must own the `from` agent (or be an admin). `weight` is clamped to [0, 1] with default 0.5. Returns 409 if an edge already exists in the same direction.

reason.description: Edge provenance. Constrained to a fixed set; an out-of-set value returns 400.

delete.description: Caller must own the source agent (`from_agent`) or be an admin. Either source or target agent id may appear in the path.

post.description:
Checks whether a given API key hash matches the key currently bound to this agent. The raw key is hashed client-side — only the hash is transmitted.

**Named agents**: hash as `SHA256(key + '|' + agentName)` before submitting.

**Public anti-impersonation check (anon-allowed).** A relying party that holds an agent's id + key can confirm the binding without being a member of the agent's org. Anonymous / cross-org callers receive **only** `bound` (the boolean leaks nothing they didn't already supply). `key_prefix` is returned **only** to callers who are members of the agent's org.

key_hash.description: First 16 hex chars of SHA256(apiKey) or SHA256(apiKey + '|' + agentName) for named agents.

bound.description: True if the submitted hash matches the registered key.

caller.description: Self-describing caller context. `key_prefix` is present iff `caller` is `org_member`; `anonymous` and `authenticated` (non-member) callers receive `{ bound, caller }` only. This is BY DESIGN, not a partial or leaky response — read `caller` instead of treating an absent `key_prefix` as a leak. The boolean `bound` is an anti-impersonation confirmation that reveals nothing the caller did not already supply.

key_prefix.description: First 16 chars of the registered key (or null if not yet captured). Returned ONLY to callers who are members of the agent's org (`caller` === `org_member`); omitted for anonymous / cross-org callers.

get.summary: Count completed ZK proofs for an agent
get.description: Public endpoint. Returns the count of `verdict_proofs` rows in `completed` state across all of the agent's checkpoints. Intended for embeddable verification widgets.

post.summary: Send a chat-native turn to the in-product Aletheia assistant.
post.description: DARK MVP (issue #2195): normalizes the chat-native `message` and runs it through the SAME answer-core the voice adapter uses, returning a chat-shaped result. Gated behind `ALETHEIA_SUPPORT_MVP_ENABLED` + the `ALETHEIA_SUPPORT_ALLOWLIST` identity allowlist (src/aletheia-support/gate.ts; defaults to the whole @mnemom.ai domain, and may be set to `*` to admit every authenticated identity) — every caller the gate doesn't allow (no user, wrong identity, or flag off) gets an identical 404, never a 401/403 that would reveal the route's existence or gating reason. Binds the real grounded answer core (`makeGroundedAnswerCore`); the fail-closed `denyAnswerCore` it originally shipped with was replaced when MNE-1937 landed.

message.description: The caller's chat turn. Must be a non-empty string.

200.description: The core's answer, chat-shaped. `refused:true` means the core (or the adapter's length guard) withheld an ungrounded answer; `answer` is then a fixed canned refusal string, never model-generated.

post.summary: Send a voice-native turn to the in-product Aletheia assistant.
post.description: DARK MVP (issue #2195): normalizes the voice-native `transcript` and runs it through the SAME answer-core the chat adapter uses, returning a voice-shaped (`speech`) result. Same gate as the chat sibling — see that operation's description. Binds the real grounded answer core (`makeGroundedAnswerCore`); the fail-closed `denyAnswerCore` it originally shipped with was replaced when MNE-1937 landed.

transcript.description: The caller's spoken turn (ASR transcript). Must be a non-empty string.

200.description: The core's answer, voice-shaped. `refused:true` means the core (or the adapter's length guard) withheld an ungrounded answer; `speech` is then a fixed canned refusal string, never model-generated.

get.summary: Check whether the caller may see the in-product Aletheia assistant (DARK MVP).
get.description: The single check the front-of-house widget polls BEFORE rendering (MNE-1930/1931) — the backend is the ONLY authority; the client never inspects the flag or allowlist itself. Reuses the exact `supportAccessAllowed` predicate `POST /v1/aletheia-support/{chat,voice}` enforce, so this can never drift out of sync with what those routes would actually allow. Unlike the chat/voice routes, ALWAYS returns 200 — the gate-check's own existence isn't sensitive (it reveals nothing about grounding/answers) — with `allowed` reflecting the real decision (`false` for flag-off, non-allowlisted, or no caller at all).

post.summary: Register an in-product Aletheia voice session (DARK)
post.description: DARK (MNE-1944): gated fail-closed by an R2 flag + allowlist, zero customer exposure until promoted. Mints an audience-scoped, short-lived `voice_grant_token` (`audience:"in_product"`) and populates the aletheia-voice per-call stash BEFORE the browser can dial Retell (register-before-dial), so a spoken turn authenticates to the governed runtime without replaying any customer or deck credential. When the flag is absent, the caller is unauthenticated, or the caller is not allowlisted, the endpoint returns an identical opaque 404 ("feature not present") and mints nothing — there is no oracle that the endpoint or a caller's allowlist status exists. Cookie/bearer-authed like any other customer route (not an `/internal/*` machine-auth surface); registered on the public spec so `preDispatchAuthGate` can classify it (issue #1519).

context.description: Optional in-product grounding/context text (KB/page context). Capped server-side. Context text ONLY — never a customer or deck credential.

200.description: Voice session registered. Returns the Retell web-call access token + call id for the browser SDK (the browser dials only after this response).

call_id.description: Retell call id the minted token is bound to.

404.description: Feature not present (DARK): flag absent, unauthenticated, or caller not allowlisted — an identical opaque response for all three (no existence / allowlist oracle).

502.description: Upstream voice provider (Retell) or the voice backend failed.

503.description: Voice is not configured on this deployment (reachable only past the flag/allowlist gate).

get.description: Returns the agent-scope alignment spec as authored. Response is content-negotiated — YAML by default, or JSON with `Accept: application/json`. parameters.name: Accept

post.summary: Explain policy evaluation for the alignment card
post.description:
Calls the policy engine in dry-run mode against the agent's composed alignment card and returns a structured trace + care-framed remediations. Optional `enrich: true` runs an LLM pass over the structured remediations to produce long-form prose; off by default. Read-style POST — no state mutation, no Idempotency-Key.

`request_snippet.tool_name` is REQUIRED and is a TOOL IDENTIFIER (`Read`, `Grep`, `Bash`) — the name matched against `capabilities.<name>.tools[]`, never a card action from `autonomy.bounded_actions` (`code_read`, `inference`). post.summary: Simulate gateway evaluation against the alignment card
post.description:
Pure-sync simulation: calls @mnemom/policy-engine twice (once with `context: "gateway"`, once with `context: "observer"`) using `dryRun: true` against the agent's current composed alignment card. Returns `{allowed, conditions, suggestions, gateway_decision, observer_assessment}`. Never crosses worker boundaries — no real gateway / observer state change.

The tools evaluated are the CALLER-supplied identifiers only — the union of `candidate_tool_call.tool_name` and every `candidate_input.messages[].toolUses[].name`, deduped. They are never read off the card (MNE-5820).

If that union is EMPTY, the request still returns **200** (unlike `explain`, which 400s), but it FAILS CLOSED: `allowed` is `"false"` with a `no_tool_named:` entry in `conditions`. The engine emits findings per tool, so a zero-length tool list would otherwise produce verdict `pass` with no violations — a green that checked nothing.

Note that `gateway_decision.verdict` and `observer_assessment.verdict` are the RAW engine output. On the zero-tool path they read `"pass"` with no violations, because the engine evaluated nothing. `allowed` — not the sub-verdicts — is this endpoint's decision field; read it.

candidate_input.description: Hypothetical conversation snippet. Any `messages[].toolUses[].name` here is a caller-supplied tool identifier and IS evaluated — unioned with `candidate_tool_call.tool_name` (MNE-5820).

candidate_tool_call.description: Hypothetical tool invocation. Synthesized into an assistant message with a toolUses block when `candidate_input.messages` is absent.

tool_name.description: A TOOL IDENTIFIER — the name a runtime invokes (`Read`, `Grep`, `Bash`), matched against `capabilities.<name>.tools[]`. NOT a card action (`code_read`, `inference`); those live in `autonomy.bounded_actions` and never match here (MNE-5820). Optional when `candidate_input.messages[].toolUses[]` names a tool instead; if NEITHER does, the response is still 200 but fails closed with `allowed: "false"`.

items.description: Array of analysis requests (same shape as POST /analyze body)

post.description: Mints a new personal API key. The full secret is returned in the `key` field — capture it now, it is not retrievable again. Scopes use the capability-based vocabulary (ADR-049); the default scope set is `["gateway", "api:read", "api:write"]`. Admin scopes (`admin:org`, `admin:platform`) are opt-in and rejected at mint time if the requester does not hold the corresponding role.

name.description: Friendly name for the key (e.g., "ci-prod", "local-dev"). Capped at 100 characters; longer names are truncated server-side.

scopes.description: Capability set for this key. If omitted, the API substitutes the default. Admin scopes (`admin:org`, `admin:platform`) are gated by the requester's current role and return HTTP 403 at mint time if the requester is not eligible.

key.description: Full secret. Capture now — never returned again.

get.summary: Inspect the calling API key (caller introspection)
get.description: Returns the resolved API key's identity: its scopes (capabilities), bound user/agent/org, and last-used metadata. Useful for clients to confirm scope and identity before issuing privileged calls.

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the API key to act on (mk-{8-hex}).

post.description: Atomically mints a replacement key with the same `name` and `scopes` as the original, then immediately revokes the old key. The full new secret is returned in the response — this is your only chance to capture it. Old key is invalid as soon as the response is returned; if you need overlap with an in-flight deploy, **create a second key first** via `POST /api-keys`, ship your code, then `DELETE` the old key. Rotation is for the suspect/compromised-key case where overlap is the opposite of what you want.

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the API key to act on (mk-{8-hex}).

201.description: New key minted, old key revoked.

key.description: Full secret. Capture now — never returned again.

get.description: Handles Supabase-hosted email links. Verifies the token via GoTrue, issues `mnemom_session` when the flow returns tokens (signup confirm, magic link), or redirects without a session for recovery flows where the SPA performs the next step.

200.description: Not emitted by this Worker: the Worker always answers with a `302`. When a client transparently follows that redirect, the SPA at the redirect target serves its HTML shell (`text/html`). Documented here so spec-conformance probes that follow the redirect don't flag the SPA landing page as an undocumented response.

302.description: Redirects to the SPA. Sets `mnemom_session` when tokens are issued.

Set-Cookie.description: Optional; only when tokens are issued.

post.summary: Exchange a cookie session for raw Supabase tokens
post.description: One-shot endpoint called by the SPA during the CLI login flow (browser → localhost handoff). Requires a valid `mnemom_session`. Returns access + refresh tokens in the JSON body. Does not modify cookies.

delete.summary: Delete authenticated user account and unlink agents

get.summary: External-SSO callback landing — issues session and redirects to SPA
get.description: MNE-1449 re-flip. Validates the HMAC-signed `mnemom_idp_initiator` cookie (CSRF), retrieves the idpIntent server-side (`POST /v2/idp_intents/{id}` with the `token`, SA-authorized), resolves the LINKED Zitadel user from the retrieve response's top-level `userId` (fail-closed 403 when the external identity is not linked — never auto-provisions), vouch-mints a first-party session, and issues `mnemom_session` via a 302 to the SPA. Returns 503 unless the cell is configured for Zitadel login.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The idpIntent id appended by Zitadel to the successUrl.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The idpIntent token appended by Zitadel to the successUrl.

302.description: Session issued. Redirects to the SPA.

get.summary: External-SSO failure landing — clears state and redirects to SPA login
get.description: MNE-1449 re-flip. The idpIntent `failureUrl`: the external IdP / Zitadel signaled a failure. No session is minted; clears the `mnemom_idp_initiator` cookie and 302-redirects to the SPA login with an error flag. Returns 503 unless the cell is configured for Zitadel login.

302.description: Redirects to the SPA login with an error flag. Clears `mnemom_idp_initiator`.

get.summary: Begin a server-orchestrated external SSO login (Zitadel idpIntent)
get.description: MNE-1449 re-flip. Server-drives the external-IdP (Microsoft Entra) login via Zitadel's idpIntent CORE API so the Zitadel hosted-login UI never renders. Starts a `POST /v2/idp_intents`, sets a short-lived `mnemom_idp_initiator` cookie (HMAC-signed state carrying the allowlisted `redirect_after` — the CSRF binding), and 302-redirects the browser to the external IdP authorize URL. DARK: returns 503 unless the cell is configured with `AUTH_PROVIDER=zitadel` + `ZITADEL_DEFAULT_IDP_ID`.

parameters.name: redirect_after
parameters.description: SPA path to land on after login completes (allowlisted).

302.description: Redirects to the external IdP authorize endpoint. Sets `mnemom_idp_initiator` cookie.

post.summary: CLI password login — returns bearer tokens in JSON body
post.description: Legacy CLI-targeted endpoint. Unlike `/auth/sign-in`, this does NOT set cookies — it returns access + refresh tokens in the JSON body for the CLI to persist at `~/.mnemom/auth.json`. For users with a ready TOTP factor the password alone does not mint tokens: the response is 200 `{ mfa_required: true, factor_id }` and no token pair is issued (aal2 step-up, #60). Rate-limited.

200.description: Tokens returned OR MFA step-up required.

mfa_token.description: Opaque, sealed, single-use step-up handle. Submit to `POST /auth/login/mfa` with the TOTP code to complete login. 10-minute TTL.

post.summary: CLI MFA step-up completion — exchange mfa_token + TOTP for tokens
post.description: Completes the aal2 step-up begun by `POST /auth/login` (which answers `200 { mfa_required, factor_id, mfa_token }` for a ready-TOTP user). The client submits the opaque `mfa_token` from that response together with the current TOTP `code`; on success the bearer token pair is returned in the JSON body, exactly like the factorless `/auth/login` 200. Cookie-free (a CLI has no cookie jar, unlike `/auth/mfa/verify`). The mfa_token is single-use and TTL-bounded. Rate-limited.

mfa_token.description: The opaque sealed handle returned by `POST /auth/login` in the mfa_required branch.

code.description: The current TOTP code for the user's ready factor.

factor_id.description: Optional factor selector. Only `totp` is supported programmatically; `email_otp` is rejected 400.

get.summary: Get authenticated user info and linked agents

put.description: Replace the authenticated user's profile avatar. The user identity is taken from the JWT/`mnm_*` auth context — there is no path parameter. Old avatar is replaced; storage cleanup happens server-side.

file.description: Avatar image. Validated for MIME type and size before upload.

avatar_url.description: Public URL of the uploaded avatar (CDN-served).

get.summary: Get the authenticated user's personal organization
get.description: Returns the authenticated user's personal organization — the auto-provisioned org-of-one that scopes their individual resources. Idempotent. If the user does not yet have a personal org (legacy account pre-dating migration 161, or a transient backfill miss), one is provisioned on the fly and `just_provisioned` is set to `true`.

just_provisioned.description: True only when this call provisioned the personal org (lazy backfill path).

post.summary: Issue a challenge for a TOTP factor
post.description: Called during the sign-in MFA step-up flow (using the `mnemom_mfa_pending` cookie) or during enrollment verification (using the existing `mnemom_session`). Returns a `challenge_id` to pass to `/auth/mfa/verify`.
Returns the TOTP secret + provisioning URI for a QR code. Factor starts in `unverified` state until `/auth/mfa/verify` is called against it.

get.summary: List the current user's TOTP factors

post.description: Requires an aal2 session (freshly MFA-verified). Returns 403 `code: aal2_required` if the session isn't aal2.

Sign-in flow: consumes the `mnemom_mfa_pending` cookie, verifies the TOTP code, and issues a full `mnemom_session`. Enrollment flow: verifies a freshly-enrolled factor using the current session and upgrades it to aal2.

200.description: Full session issued. Response sets `mnemom_session` cookie.

get.summary: OIDC callback landing — issues session and redirects to SPA
get.description: B1 PR-B (MNE-1449). Validates the HMAC-signed `state` (double-submitted against the `mnemom_oidc_initiator` cookie), consumes the single-use nonce, exchanges the authorization `code` at the Zitadel token endpoint (PKCE), and issues `mnemom_session` via a 302 to the SPA. Returns 503 unless the cell is configured for Zitadel login.

302.description: Session issued. Redirects to the SPA.

post.summary: Finalize an inbound loginV2 auth request against the caller's session
post.description: loginV2 finalize. id.mnemom.ai has no hosted loginV2 UI, so the mnemom login page is the loginV2 `baseUri` target: after it authenticates the user (issuing the `__Host-mnemom_session` cookie), it posts the inbound Zitadel auth-request id here. The endpoint reuses the caller's stashed Zitadel login session (falling back to a fresh user-only vouch session if that has aged past `passwordCheckLifetime`) to finalize the request, returning the RP `callbackUrl` for the browser to follow. Requires an authenticated session cookie; the `authRequestId` must resolve to an allowed first-party client. Returns 503 unless the cell is configured with `AUTH_PROVIDER=zitadel`.

authRequestId.description: The inbound Zitadel V2 auth-request handle (`V2_<id>`).

200.description: The auth request was finalized; follow the returned callback URL.

callbackUrl.description: The RP callback URL carrying the authorization `code`.

get.summary: Begin an OIDC authorization-code login (Zitadel redirect leg)
get.description: B1 PR-B (MNE-1449). Generates PKCE + an HMAC-signed state + single-use nonce, sets a short-lived `mnemom_oidc_initiator` cookie, and 302-redirects the browser to the Zitadel hosted-login authorize endpoint. Plumbing for hosted-login / enterprise SSO (PR-E). Returns 503 unless the cell is configured with `AUTH_PROVIDER=zitadel` + the login-client config.

parameters.name: redirect_after
parameters.description: SPA path to land on after login completes (allowlisted).

302.description: Redirects to the Zitadel authorize endpoint. Sets `mnemom_oidc_initiator` cookie.

post.summary: Begin passkey sign-in — return WebAuthn assertion options
post.description: Unauthenticated. Returns `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions` with an empty `allowCredentials` list (discoverable-credentials flow). The browser surfaces any matching passkey for this RP without needing the user to enter an email. Rate-limited.

post.summary: Begin passkey enrollment — return WebAuthn creation options
post.description: Authenticated endpoint. Returns `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions` for the SPA to pass to `navigator.credentials.create()`. Stores the challenge in KV with a 30-second TTL; the companion `/verify-enroll` endpoint consumes it. `excludeCredentials` is pre-populated with the user's existing passkeys so the authenticator prevents duplicate enrollment of the same key.

200.description: WebAuthn creation options. Shape follows the WebAuthn Level 3 spec.

post.summary: Verify a passkey assertion and issue a session
post.description: Unauthenticated. Consumes the challenge issued by `/auth/passkey/challenge`, verifies the assertion via `@simplewebauthn/server`, mints Supabase tokens via `admin.generateLink(magiclink)` for the resolved user (same pattern T3-2c uses for SSO identity linking), and issues `mnemom_session` with `auth_method: 'passkey'`. Counter is enforced monotonically — a decrement rejects the assertion.

post.summary: Verify a passkey registration response + persist the credential
post.description: Authenticated endpoint. Consumes the challenge issued by `/auth/passkey/enroll`, verifies the attestation via `@simplewebauthn/server`, and inserts a row into `user_passkeys`. A user-supplied `friendly_name` is stored alongside for UI display.

get.summary: List the current user's enrolled passkeys
get.description: Returns the safe subset of `user_passkeys` for the authenticated user (omits public_key, counter, last_used_ip).

delete.description: Requires aal2. Deleting a passkey does not affect other passkeys or the password/MFA fallback; those remain usable.

post.description: Authenticated password update. Used by both the `/reset-password` recovery flow (after the recovery email callback issues a session) and voluntary password changes from account settings. Cookie session auth required (`mnemom_session`); bearer tokens are not accepted on this route. After a successful update, every other session for the same user is revoked with audit reason `password_reset`.

password.description: New password. Must be at least 12 characters. The upstream identity provider applies additional weak-password and breach-list checks; failures surface as 400 with a `password_rejected` error code.

200.description: Password updated. Other sessions for the same user are revoked best-effort.

post.description: Always returns 200 on 4xx upstream responses (to avoid user enumeration). 5xx upstream errors surface as 5xx to the caller.

redirect_to.description: Allowlisted SPA path to return to after the user clicks the reset link.

post.description: Legacy CLI-targeted refresh grant. Trades a refresh token for a new access + refresh token pair. Rate-limited.
Re-sends the signup confirmation email for a pending account.

get.description: Minimal whoami endpoint. Returns `{ user }` when the `mnemom_session` cookie is valid; returns 401 otherwise. Preferred over `GET /auth/me` for cookie-only browser sessions — `/auth/me` is bearer-only and preserves its legacy response shape unchanged.

Returns every non-revoked session for the authenticated user. Each row is safe to render in an "Active sessions" UI — no tokens are disclosed. The session matching the request cookie is marked `is_current: true`, and sessions originating from the same hashed source IP as the current request are marked `same_network_as_current: true`. See ADR-028.

200.description: Active sessions for the current user.

sid.description: Opaque session id. Pass to `DELETE /auth/sessions/{sid}` to revoke.

device_label.description: Best-effort human label derived from the original User-Agent and IP at sign-in time (e.g. "Safari on macOS — San Francisco").

is_current.description: True for the session tied to the request cookie.

same_network_as_current.description: True when this session's hashed source IP matches the current request's.

delete.description: Revokes every active session for the current user _except_ the one making this call. Requires aal2 (MFA-verified session). Sessions issued before per-session revocation (v=1 cookies) cannot identify themselves as "current" and receive `409 legacy_session_requires_reauth` — the user must sign in again to use this action. See ADR-028.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional idempotency key; repeated calls with the same key return the same result within 24 hours.

revoked.description: Count of sessions revoked (excludes the current session).

post.summary: Revoke a session using a signed email token
post.description: Consumes a signed token minted at email-send time by the new-device notification flow. Possession of the token is the auth factor — no existing session cookie is required, no MFA. Returns 200 on any verified-valid token even if the underlying sid is already revoked (idempotent, non-enumerating). Returns 400 on malformed, tampered, expired, or key-mismatched tokens. Public endpoint, rate-limited. See ADR-031.

token.description: HS256-signed token from the new-device email link.

200.description: Session revocation accepted (idempotent — 200 returned even if the session was already gone).

delete.description: Revokes one non-current session by its `sid`. The KV blocklist is updated so the gateway rejects the next request bearing that session on its next hit. Cannot be used to revoke the session making this request — use `POST /auth/sign-out` for that. Requires aal2. Idempotent: a sid that is already revoked or never belonged to the user returns 404 (non-enumeration). See ADR-028.

parameters.name: sid
parameters.description: Session identifier returned by `GET /auth/sessions`.

post.summary: Set the authenticated user's preferred email locale
post.description: Updates `user_metadata.locale` on the Supabase auth user. Locale-aware send paths (billing webhooks, licensing expiry, auth send-email-hook) read this field to choose between English (default), French, German, Italian, and Spanish copy. Cookie session auth required; the change is effective immediately for subsequent email sends.

locale.description: Preferred email locale. Values outside this enum are rejected with `unsupported_locale`.

post.description: Server-enforces SSO for org-enforced domains (returns 403 with `code: sso_required`). For users with a verified TOTP factor, returns 200 `{ mfa_required: true, factor_id }` and sets a short-lived `mnemom_mfa_pending` cookie; otherwise issues `mnemom_session` and returns `{ user }`.

200.description: Full session issued OR MFA step-up required.

Set-Cookie.description: `mnemom_session` on full session, or `mnemom_mfa_pending` on MFA step-up.

post.summary: Sign out and clear session cookies
post.description: Revokes the refresh token upstream and clears `mnemom_session` + `mnemom_mfa_pending`. Idempotent and anon-callable by design — calling it without a session returns 200 + no-op cookie clear, so a logged-out client can safely re-issue the call without observing a 401.

Creates a new user account. When email confirmation is required on the Supabase project, returns `{ user, email_confirmation_required: true }` without issuing a session cookie; the user must click the email link. When auto-confirm is on, issues `mnemom_session` and returns `{ user }`. If the email already has an account, returns `409` with `code: email_exists` — no duplicate account is created and no verification email is sent (MNE-1348).

redirect_to.description: Allowlisted SPA path to return to after email confirmation.

200.description: Account created. Either returns a full session (auto-confirm) or awaits email confirmation.

user.description: `null` while email confirmation is pending — no session is issued until the user clicks the confirmation link.

get.summary: IdP callback landing — issues session and redirects to SPA
get.description: Validates the HMAC-signed state (from the `mnemom_sso_initiator` cookie), consumes the single-use nonce, exchanges the PKCE code, enforces domain + org binding, performs SSO identity linking (T3-2c), and issues `mnemom_session` via a 302 to the SPA's `redirect_after` path.

302.description: Session issued. Redirects to the SPA.

get.summary: Check if email domain has SSO enabled

post.description: Looks up the SSO provider for the email's domain, generates PKCE + HMAC-signed state, sets a short-lived `mnemom_sso_initiator` cookie, and returns the IdP URL for the SPA to `window.location.href` to.

redirect_after.description: SPA path to return to after SSO completes (allowlisted).

200.description: IdP URL returned. Also sets `mnemom_sso_initiator` cookie.

post.summary: Exchange a GoTrue refresh token for a mnemom_session cookie
post.description: Mirror of `/auth/cli-exchange` in the opposite direction. Called by the SPA after landing on a Supabase implicit-flow redirect (magic-link login), whose session tokens arrive in the URL fragment. The endpoint performs the GoTrue refresh grant server-side — proving possession and consuming the single-use refresh token — then registers a session and sets the HttpOnly `mnemom_session` cookie. JSON-only; no redirect parameter. Rate-limited like sibling auth endpoints.

refresh_token.description: GoTrue refresh token from the implicit-flow fragment.

threshold_cents.description: Legacy single-scalar field, preserved for back-compat clients: the lowest configured `thresholds[].value_cents`, or `null` if no thresholds are configured.

thresholds.description: Ordered (ascending by `value_cents`) severity-tiered threshold set (D5 alert hardening). The legacy scalar, if set and no multi-threshold set is configured, is lifted into a single-entry `warning` set here for backward compatibility.

fired_levels.description: Severity levels already fired (and deduped) for the current threshold configuration.

schema.description: Two accepted shapes: (a) NEW — `thresholds`: an ordered severity-tiered set (empty array clears it); (b) LEGACY — `threshold_cents`: the single scalar. `thresholds` takes precedence when present; either write resets per-threshold and legacy dedup state.

thresholds.description: New multi-threshold set. Each entry accepts `level` (`warning`|`urgent`|`depleted`, must be unique and rise in severity with value), `value` (non-negative number), an optional `unit` (`cents`, default, or `mu` — 1 µ = 1¢, exact conversion), and an optional `message` (<=500 chars). An empty array clears the configured set.

threshold_cents.description: On the multi-threshold write path this mirrors the lowest configured `thresholds[].value_cents` (`null` if the set was cleared); on the legacy write path this echoes the submitted scalar.

thresholds.description: Present on the multi-threshold write path: the normalized, stored threshold set.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD)

get.summary: Get plan feature flags for authenticated user
Get the caller's org mu-engine balance
get.description: Returns the mu (metered-unit) ledger balance for the authenticated caller's organization, augmented with enforcement status if the org runs enforce-configured agents (MNE-6915). Requires JWT auth; RBAC is enforced by api before forwarding — the caller must be a member of the target org (defaults to their primary org; an explicit `org_id` query targets a specific org and a non-member is denied 403). api resolves the org's `billing_account_id` server-side, queries the org's agents to determine enforcement configuration, and augments the upstream mnemom-mu balance response with `effectiveMode` ('enforce' | 'passthrough') and `enforcementPausedReason` ('balance_depleted' | null) before returning. A client-supplied account id is never used. 503 when the mnemom-mu binding/URL is unconfigured (fail-closed).

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Target org id. Defaults to the caller's primary org. A caller who is not a member of this org is denied 403.

200.description: mu ledger balance for the org with enforcement status augmentation. Response includes all upstream mnemom-mu balance fields plus optional enforcement fields (effectiveMode, enforcementPausedReason) if the org runs enforce-configured agents.

get.summary: Read the caller's org mu ledger entries
get.description: The customer's own mu account statement: every ledger entry (grant / hold / settle / release / burn / refund / adjustment) with its `lot_allocations` provenance and entry hash. This is what makes purchase RECEIPTS and itemized usage possible — a balance without it is a number with no explanation behind it. Identical org-context + RBAC discipline to `GET /billing/mu`: RBAC is enforced before any read, and the account id is the SERVER-RESOLVED `billing_account_id`, never client-supplied (a NULL one is 409, matching the balance route rather than falling back to a personal account the way the internal resolver does). `cursor` / `from` / `to` / `limit` pass through verbatim to the frozen mnemom-mu upstream `GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/ledger`, which bounds `limit` itself (default 100, max 500). Read-only by construction: api presents its own `mu:check` service key, which carries no spend or grant scope. 503 when the mnemom-mu binding/URL is unconfigured (fail-closed).

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Target org id. Defaults to the caller's primary org. A caller who is not a member of this org is denied 403.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque sequence cursor from a previous page's `nextCursor`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on entry creation time (ISO-8601).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on entry creation time (ISO-8601).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Upstream clamps to 1..500 (default 100).

200.description: A page of ledger entries plus `nextCursor` (mnemom-mu response, passed through verbatim).

get.summary: Read the caller's org mnemom-native monthly usage statement
get.description: The mnemom-NATIVE monthly usage statement for the authenticated caller's organization — the itemized statement mnemom itself produces from its OWN ledger (`mu_view_statement_lines`), independent of Stripe's hosted invoice PDF. This is what backs the first-party downloadable PDF/CSV: a customer can obtain a record of their metered usage even when they have no Stripe invoices at all (the common prepay case). Same org-context + RBAC discipline as `GET /billing/mu`: RBAC is enforced before any read, and the account id is the SERVER-RESOLVED `billing_account_id`, never client-supplied. `period` is a required `YYYY-MM` month. READ-ONLY by construction: api presents its own `mu:check` service key, which carries no spend or grant scope, and the statement is a pure projection of already-recorded usage — nothing is minted or mutated. Forwards to the frozen mnemom-billing upstream `GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/statement`; the `{accountId, period, lines, totalUsd}` body is passed through verbatim. 503 when the mnemom-mu binding/URL is unconfigured (fail-closed).

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Target org id. Defaults to the caller's primary org. A caller who is not a member of this org is denied 403.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: The statement month, as `YYYY-MM` (UTC-keyed, matching the ledger).

200.description: The native monthly statement (mnemom-billing response, passed through verbatim): `{accountId, period, lines, totalUsd}`.

get.summary: List the organization's saved payment instruments
get.description: Returns kind, brand, last four, expiry, verification status and default flag ONLY. A full card or bank account number is never returned by this API. Owner/admin only; the organization is resolved from the session (an explicit org_id must be one the caller is a member of).

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Target organization. Omit to use the caller's own organization. Membership is enforced, so this cannot be used to read another organization's instruments.

200.description: Saved payment instruments, tokenized fields only.

delete.description: Owner-only. Detaches the instrument from the organization's Stripe customer. An instrument that does not belong to the resolved organization returns the same 404 as one that does not exist, so this cannot be used to probe another organization. Removing the current default is refused with 409 while other instruments remain — set a new default first.

post.summary: Choose which saved instrument gets charged
post.description: Owner-only. Points the organization's Stripe customer at this instrument for future invoices, and returns the full updated list so the caller never has to infer the new default.

200.description: Updated instrument list, with the new default flagged.

post.summary: Reactivate a subscription scheduled for cancellation

get.description: Completed μ prepay purchases for the caller's organization, as receipts. The prepay counterpart of GET /billing/invoices: a prepay customer has receipts and no invoices. Requires org owner or admin.

get.summary: Get usage metrics for current user

schema.description: `handleGetMyAgentUsage` returns the `get_user_agent_usage` RPC result, an object keyed by `agents` — not a bare array.

agents.description: Per-agent usage rows for the requested window.

get.description: Returns the ORG-WIDE µ spend total — the sum of all members' consumption over the requested lookback window. Each endpoint returns a RATE-CARD ESTIMATE (not the authoritative account-scoped ledger burn) derived from token counts, since usage_events stores no cost column — the response carries `basis: "rate_card_estimate"` and every µ field is named `estimated_*`. µ is the display unit (1 µ = 1¢ = 1000 mmu). Requires org owner, admin, or auditor. Feature-gated by `ORG_TOTAL_SPEND_ENABLED`; returns 404 to every caller (before auth) while the flag is off.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Target organization ID.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Lookback window in days. One of 7, 30, 90.

200.description: Organization-wide spend total (estimated) for the window.

totals_unavailable.description: True if the window-totals aggregation failed.

get.summary: Get the signed-in user's own per-turn µ spend (D5 per-user visibility)
get.description: Returns the CURRENT user's own per-turn spend, self-scoped by session `sub` only — there is no person_id parameter and a user can never read another person's turns. Each turn's µ value is a RATE-CARD ESTIMATE derived from token counts (usage_events stores no cost), NOT the authoritative account-scoped ledger burn — the response carries `basis: "rate_card_estimate"` and every µ field is named `estimated_*`. µ is the display unit (1 µ = 1¢ = 1000 mmu). Feature-gated by `USAGE_SELF_SPEND_API_ENABLED`; returns 404 to every caller (before auth) while the flag is off.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Lookback window in days. One of 7, 30, 90.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max turns per page (clamped to 200).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque keyset cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor`.

200.description: The user's own per-turn spend (estimated) for the window.

basis.description: Always `rate_card_estimate` — the µ figures are derived from token counts, not the settled ledger burn.

estimated_mmu.description: Estimated spend in integer mmu (1 µ = 1000 mmu).

estimated_mu.description: Estimated spend as a µ decimal string.

get.summary: Is Mnemom Agent enabled for this organization?
get.description: The `mnemom agent` feature gate. Enabled when the caller's email is in the internal cohort (`@mnemom.ai`), the caller is Mnemom staff, or the org (or the caller's own account) holds a `product_access_grant` for product `code` — typically from a redeemed Code invitation (`POST /v1/invites/accept`). `org_id` targets a specific org the caller belongs to; omitted, the caller's primary org is used. A non-member of `org_id` is 403 (`forbidden`); an org without access is 403 `code_not_enabled` with a machine-readable hint the CLI prints.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Target organization (defaults to the caller's primary org).

200.description: Mnemom Agent is enabled for the org.

source.description: Why access is enabled: internal cohort (@mnemom.ai email), platform staff, or a product-access grant (redeemed invitation / staff-granted).

True only for the internal cohort and platform staff; invited customers run terminal-only. The CLI reads this to gate its `--remote-control`/`--server` shapes and the auto-upgrade.

post.summary: Mint a single-use coherence claim-intent ticket (anonymous).
post.description: The coherence report-claim flow (MNE-1379). A LOGGED-OUT viewer of a Coherence report who clicks "Claim your report" and creates an account receives a short-lived, single-use, opaque ticket (`mci_…`) scope-bound to `{report_slug, intent: enroll_passkey}`. That ticket — NOT a session token or cookie — is the only value that rides the sign-up → email-confirm → return round-trip on the URL, so nothing sensitive lands in the URL, the confirmation email, or browser localStorage. There is NO proof at mint: the report is publicly viewable (the slug is not a secret), so the authorization for the claim is the email-confirmation round-trip the user must complete to reach the authed exchange (proof of control of the email the report binds to). Intentionally public (`security: []`), the same posture as `/dojo/claim-intent`. Exchange the ticket via `POST /coherence/claim-intent/exchange` once authenticated.

report_slug.description: The Coherence report slug to bind the claim to (16 URL-safe chars). Carried through the round-trip so the claim page can resume the ceremony on the authenticated return.

intent_token.description: Opaque single-use ticket (`mci_…`). Present it to the exchange. Never a session token.

post.description: The freshly-authenticated first-timer — returned to the claim page by the email-confirmation callback, which set the HttpOnly mnemom_session cookie this exchange resolves SERVER-SIDE — presents the ticket minted by `POST /coherence/claim-intent`. The ticket is atomically consumed (single-use) and the scope-bound `{report_slug, intent}` is returned so the claim page can resume the enroll → step-up → claim ceremony with a REAL session (instead of the doomed immediate enroll that 401'd). The session is the only authority here — never a token on the URL. MNE-1379.

intent_token.description: The opaque single-use ticket (`mci_…`) from the mint step.

200.description: The scope-bound claim target to resume.

post.summary: Proxied HubSpot Forms submission (non-enterprise contact + newsletter)
post.description: Server-side replacement for the old browser→HubSpot Forms submission. Routes /contact (general/support/privacy) and newsletter signups through the Worker so they're gated by the anti-spam guard (honeypot + strict email/char/length validation + optional Cloudflare Turnstile verification) before anything reaches HubSpot. `form_type=contact` requires a Turnstile token (once `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` is set on the Worker); `form_type=newsletter` runs honeypot + validation only. On success the Worker also performs the CRM upsert + hot-lead Slack alert (same as /contact/notify). Returns a non-2xx so the UI can keep the form open on rejection.

Reconstructs the decision from its row and delegates to the shared verifySafeHouseDecision core: a tampered covered field or prev_hash breaks the chain recompute; a forged/absent-key signature breaks the Ed25519 check — both surface as verified:false (a successful answer, not an error). post.summary: Mint a single-use claim-intent ticket (anonymous, birth-token proof).
post.description: The true-first-timer claim flow (MNE-879). A LOGGED-OUT user who opens a dojo claim link proves ownership with the birth token (`mnbt_…`) / hash proof and receives a short-lived, single-use, opaque ticket (`mci_…`). That ticket — NOT the secret proof — rides the sign-up → email-confirm → return round-trip, so nothing sensitive lands in the URL, the confirmation email, or browser localStorage (which is gone when the email opens on another device — the exact reason a first-timer claimed an agent but it never bound to its dojo config). The proof is verified HERE and never stored; the ticket is the post-verification capability. Intentionally public (`security: []`) — the birth-token proof IS the authorization, the same posture as `/dojo/try-me/resolve`. Exchange the ticket via `POST /dojo/claim-intent/exchange` once authenticated.

hash_proof.description: Ownership proof — the live birth token (`mnbt_…`) whose row pins this agent's hash, or the full 64-hex `SHA-256(apiKey|name)` proof. Verified at mint; never stored.

dojo_config_id.description: Optional — the TryMeConfig to bind the agent to at exchange (the claim link's `&dojo_config`). Carried through the round-trip so the bind can't be lost.

intent_token.description: Opaque single-use ticket (`mci_…`). Present it to the exchange.

post.summary: Exchange a claim-intent ticket — claim + bind (authed).
post.description: The freshly-authenticated first-timer presents the ticket minted by `POST /dojo/claim-intent`. The ticket is atomically consumed (single-use), the agent is claimed into the caller's PERSONAL org (dojo invites are personal by design — the same claim-to-org core as `POST /agents/{id}/claim`, with NO re-proof: the ticket is the capability), and the agent is bound to its dojo config — the step that silently no-op'd before, leaving the agent claimed but invisible in the dojo. One server-side operation replaces the fragile claim→link→bind dance. MNE-879.

intent_token.description: The opaque single-use ticket (`mci_…`) from the mint step.

bound.description: Whether the agent was bound to a dojo config (false if the ticket carried none).

bind_error.description: Present ONLY when a dojo config was named and the bind did not land — names WHY, so a `bound:false` is diagnosable instead of silent. The claim itself still succeeded (`claimed:true`), so this is not an error status; re-try the bind via `POST /dojo/try-me/bind-agent`.

post.summary: Mint an ephemeral compute/operate key (gateway + api:read + api:write).
post.description: Mints a Mnemom-provided, ephemeral API key carrying `gateway` + `api:read` + `api:write` (the standard-key default; no admin scopes), hung off the dedicated `dojo-system` billing account (not tied to ownership). `gateway` lets the runner act AS the agent through the prod gateway; `api:read`/`api:write` let the agent authenticate to mnemom-api MCP routes during onboarding (BE BORN / DECLARE) — a `gateway`-only key would 401 on every MCP call. The cleartext key is returned ONCE. Optionally bound to a TryMeConfig (sets its `compute_key_ref`). Admin-only — backs the `/admin/dojo` control surface. MNE-517 §2 / MNE-519.

Backs the `/dashboard/dojo` visibility gate (`dojo_enabled` = owns ≥1) AND the agent selector (`agents`). Pass `org_id` to scope to the active org's fleet (ADR-062) — the dashboard does this so the dojo only shows under an org where you own a dojo agent; omit it for the legacy org-agnostic listing. No admin bypass — visibility derives purely from owning a dojo agent. MNE-517.

The cleartext is AES-256-GCM-encrypted at rest and resolved server-side ONLY (`resolveDojoProviderKey`); it is NEVER returned. Admin-only — backs `/admin/dojo`. MNE-517 (BYOK pivot).

post.summary: Verify a Dojo completion receipt against the published JWKS.
post.description: PUBLIC — in-band Ed25519 verification of a posted completion-receipt JWS against the CURRENTLY published JWKS (`/v1/.well-known/jwks.json`; active + retired-window keys). Returns the structured verdict (`valid`, `payload`, `key_id`, `errors`). A bad / tampered / expired receipt is `valid:false` with the failing checks enumerated — the endpoint itself is still 200 (the verification ran). 'Verify, don't trust': the same check can be run offline against the public key. MNE-802.

payload.description: The receipt's decoded payload. On `valid:true` this is a full `DojoCompletionReceipt/v1` payload (the shape of `receiptResponseSchema.payload`). On `valid:false` it is the BEST-EFFORT decoded payload — untrusted and possibly partial or arbitrary (whatever the presented, unverified JWS decoded to) — echoed for diagnostics, so it is intentionally NOT constrained to the strict receipt shape (a tampered/bogus receipt must still surface as a 200 `valid:false`, never a 500). `null` when the JWS could not be parsed at all.

get.description: PUBLIC — the `session_id` is the credential (a shareable permalink). Returns the Ed25519-signed completion receipt for a COMPLETED dojo try-me run: it declares the agent's alignment/protection cards (by canonical content-hash) and the Safe House (sparring) verdict, plus a verify pointer. The receipt is DERIVED deterministically from the completed session + its scenario (not stored) and is independently verifiable against the published JWKS. Reveals only the shareable claim — no raw transcript/event stream (that stays behind the owner-gated `/sim/{id}/export`). 409 if the run hasn't completed; 503 if signing isn't configured. MNE-802.

A SEPARATE, dojo-specific step the agent performs AFTER `mnemom login` — NOT part of the canonical claim flow (that page is untouched). AUTHED + owner-only: the caller must authenticate (Bearer/API key — the agent uses its `mnemom login` session) AND be a member of the agent's governing org (ADR-062 — the same gate as `put_alignment_by_agent`/DECLARE). `config_id` (baked into the manifest's `bind` block + the claim link's `&dojo_config`) is the unambiguous selector vs the burned token. Bounded against abuse: the config must be opt-in `self_serve_resettable`, the reset count is hard-capped, and a token is re-armable only while already burned (never multiplies a live token) — all enforced atomically. The 409 is uniform across every not-resettable reason (unknown / not opt-in / still live / over cap) so it is not an enumeration or state oracle. POST (body `{token}`) is equivalent. MNE-800.

get.summary: Resolve a single-use Try-Me token to its onboarding briefing manifest.
get.description: UNAUTHED — the token IS the credential. Returns the briefing manifest, a declarative state machine an agent executes deterministically: it leads with a machine-readable `directive` (fetch the RAW JSON, do not summarize), declares the flow as explicit states (orient → resolve → birth → claim → spar → receipt), and declares BOTH owner-tier auth doors (`auth_doors`: an RFC 6750 MCP step-up challenge and an RFC 8628 device authorization grant) so the agent negotiates by host capability. The agent is born through the gateway with a per-session BIRTH TOKEN (`mnbt_…`, MNE-799 server-mediated birth) and a CONCRETE model id; the gateway resolves the birth token server-side to the real key and mints a server-side `mnm-…` agent_id, and the agent's identity is token-derived (`first16hex(SHA256(birth_token))`), NOT name-derived — no shared provider key is ever handed to the agent (the name is only a display label). The human takes ownership via the canonical /claim URL (the claim page is generic and untouched), then — as the human, via a `mnemom login` CLI session — the agent records itself with the Dojo (a SEPARATE authed, owner-only bind) and DECLARES ITS OWN GOOD alignment + protection cards (`mnemom card/protection publish`, nudge). Single-use: preconditions (live token, provider key configured, scenario present, birth token minted) are checked BEFORE the atomic burn, so a setup slip returns a clean error WITHOUT consuming the token; the burn is the last step. Idempotent within a reuse window (MNE-800): a re-resolve of a recently-burned token replays the EXACT manifest (same birth token) instead of 410. A second resolve outside the window returns 404/410. POST (body `{token}`) is equivalent, and the MCP `get_started(token)` tool returns the identical manifest over MCP. MNE-517 / MNE-799 / MNE-798.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The single-use Try-Me token (e.g. `wndrco`).

200.description: The briefing manifest for the burned token.

directive.description: MNE-798 — the FIRST manifest field: the machine-readable contract (fetch the RAW JSON, do not summarize, agent-directive language — never 'visit'). Hoisted to the top so a summarizing reader hits it before stripping the structured fields.

human_beats.description: MNE-804 — the claim-first arc as the human FEELS it: exactly three one-click beats (name → authorize → Begin Sim). post.description: Starts a claim on a registrable apex domain you own and returns the DNS TXT record to place (`mnemom-verification=<token>`). Idempotent per (owner, domain): re-POSTing the same domain returns the same pending token. Subdomains, IP literals and non-apex hosts are rejected. Rate-limited per user and per IP.

200.description: Claim created or idempotently re-fetched; TXT record returned.

verification.description: Everything needed to place the DNS TXT record at the domain apex.

name.description: DNS record name (apex = `@`).

get.description: Returns the caller's domain claims with status, verification time, Honor Roll opt-in, public response note, and the latest isittrustready.ai scan `grade` (fetched and cached server-side; `null` when the domain has not been scanned or the scanner is unreachable).

put.summary: Opt a verified domain in/out of the Honor Roll
put.description: Sets explicit, revocable Honor Roll consent for a verified domain. Verified claims only (409 otherwise).

get.summary: Public claim status (no auth, no PII)
get.description: Credential-free, cacheable projection consumed by the isittrustready.ai scanner. Always returns 200; an unknown or unverified domain yields `claimed:false`. Contains ZERO PII — only `domain`, `claimed`, `honor_roll`, and the owner-published `response_note`. `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`.

put.summary: Set a verified domain's public owner response
put.description: Publishes a plain-text owner response (≤500 chars; control and bidi/zero-width characters are stripped server-side) rendered on the public scan report. Verified claims only (409 otherwise). An empty note clears it.

post.summary: Verify a domain claim via DNS TXT
post.description: Looks up the apex TXT records over a fixed DoH resolver (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1) for `mnemom-verification=<token>`. Found → the claim is marked verified. Not found → `{claimed:false, reason:"txt-not-found"}` (HTTP 200; retry after DNS propagation). A successful verify by a different owner transfers control (anti-squat). Rate-limited per user and per IP.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The registrable apex being verified.

200.description: Verification result (verified, or a friendly retryable not-found).

post.description: Ingest a single piece of in-product feedback (compliment / problem / suggestion) from an authenticated user (web app) or agent (MCP/gateway). Reporter-supplied content is redacted (email / API-key / JWT / phone / long-hex shapes replaced with `[redacted:*]`) BEFORE storage, and the sensitive context fields (`ai_prompts`, `diagnostics`) are dropped unless the matching consent flag is set. Idempotent: a replayed request carrying the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the same `feedback_id` and creates no duplicate row. Inherits the standard per-IP REST rate limit.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated key (e.g. a UUID). Replaying the same key within 24h returns the original response unchanged.

consent_prompts.description: When true, `context_bundle.ai_prompts` is stored (redacted); otherwise it is dropped.

consent_diagnostics.description: When true, `context_bundle.diagnostics` is stored (redacted); otherwise it is dropped.

consent_contact.description: When true, the reporter opts in to a resolution-email notification.

context_bundle.description: Optional diagnostic context. `route_url` and `breadcrumbs` are always redacted-and-stored; `ai_prompts` / `diagnostics` are consent-gated.

route_url.description: App route the reporter was on.

breadcrumbs.description: Recent UI actions (roles/test-ids only, never raw input).

attachment_ids.description: IDs of previously-presigned pending attachments to bind to this submission.

company_website.description: Honeypot — must be empty. Any non-empty value silently accepts and persists nothing.

feedback_id.description: The stored submission id (absent on a honeypot-silent accept).

post.summary: Get a presigned upload URL for a feedback attachment (MNE-1659)
post.description: Issues a presigned R2 PUT URL for a screenshot/screen-recording attachment and records a `pending` feedback_attachments row for it — the client uploads the bytes DIRECTLY to R2 with this URL (the worker never proxies them), then passes the returned `attachment_id` in `POST /feedback`'s `attachment_ids` array to bind it to the real submission. No owner column exists on feedback_attachments yet, so ownership is stamped into the R2 object key namespace instead of a DB column. A row that is never bound (upload abandoned, or the follow-up POST /feedback never happens) is reclaimed by a sweep cron past a 1h grace window. Returns 503 if R2 presign credentials aren't provisioned for this env.

content_type.description: MIME type of the attachment. Must match migration 397's feedback_attachments_content_type_ck exactly.

size_bytes.description: Declared size in bytes; 25MB cap. Advisory only — R2 does not enforce this against the actual PUT.

attachment_id.description: Pass this in POST /feedback's attachment_ids to bind it.

upload_url.description: Presigned R2 PUT URL. PUT the raw bytes here directly.

headers.description: Headers the client must send with the PUT (Content-Type).

expires_in.description: Seconds until the presigned URL expires.

503.description: Attachment upload not configured for this environment.

post.description: Receives Issue state-change events from Linear (MNE-1680). When a linked issue (matched via the `Feedback-ID:` marker MNE-1679 embeds in the issue body, resolved through `feedback_work_items.linear_issue_id`) moves to a completed state (Done / Released), writes a `feedback_resolutions` row and flips the submission — and any cluster-dupe submissions — to resolved. Non-issue events, non-completed states, and issues with no linked work item are acknowledged as no-ops (200). Authenticated by the `linear-signature` header, an HMAC-SHA-256 digest of the raw request body keyed on `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET`, timing-safe-compared. FAILS CLOSED: if that secret is not configured, every request is rejected — this endpoint never silently skips signature validation. Handler: `handleLinearWebhook` in `src/feedback/linear-webhook.ts`; `runLinearReconciler` is the scheduled backstop for dropped deliveries.

post.summary: Grant the caller's account its one-time starter μ balance, IF its contract is signed
post.description: Contract-gated, idempotent starter-balance grant (MNE-6427). api authenticates the caller (JWT), resolves their OWN org and billing account server-side (no client-supplied account/org/amount is honored — MNE-441 self-provisioning), and reads the contract gate from mnemom-billing's `GET /v1/contracts` (mu:check). If NO contract has `signedOffAt` set, returns 200 `{granted:false, reason:"contract_not_signed"}` and mints nothing. If a contract IS signed, forwards to billing's idempotent `POST /v1/internal/accounts/{id}/intro-grant` (mu:grant) and passes its result through verbatim — `{granted:true, mmu}` on first grant, `{granted:false, reason:"already_granted"}` on replay (billing dedupes on a key shared with retail card capture and personal-org signup, so the grant lands at most once per account). Fails CLOSED (503) whenever the gate cannot be verified — read/grant identity unset, or the contracts read errors — never a silent grant. "api never grants" (MNE-2516) holds by credential scope and a server-authored upstream body; api performs no ledger arithmetic and owns no amount.

200.description: Grant outcome, mnemom-billing's result passed through verbatim: `{granted:true, mmu}` when the starter balance was seeded, `{granted:false, reason:"already_granted"}` on an idempotent replay, or `{granted:false, reason:"contract_not_signed"}` when the account has no signed-off contract (no money moved).

Handles `installation` (created/deleted/suspend/unsuspend/new_permissions_accepted) and `installation_repositories` (added/removed) for installations already bound to a Mnemom org; `deleted` also revokes every open token grant. Everything else is acknowledged and ignored. Handler: `handleGithubWebhook` in `src/org/github-federation.ts`.
