Admin-only (mnemom_staff). 404 if `id` doesn't exist. MNE-7094.

post.description: RG M1 invite flow (MNE-7166). Redeems an opaque `pinv_…` invite token: validates the token, marks the `product_invite` `accepted` exactly-once, grants the invitee access to the invited product(s), and forwards the staged starter-µ grant to billing server-side. Invitee-facing and authenticated — a user invite requires the caller to be that user (403 otherwise); an org invite requires the caller to be an owner/admin of that org. Idempotent: a second accept re-asserts access and returns 200 without re-firing the grant. The grant amount is admin-only and never appears in the request or response — the response only reports whether the starter grant `fired` or was `deferred`.

token.description: The opaque `pinv_…` invite token from the accept link.

200.description: Invite accepted (or already accepted). Product access is granted; the response reports whether the starter grant fired or was deferred. Never carries the grant amount.

accepted.description: True once the invite is in the accepted state.

already_accepted.description: Present and true when the invite was already accepted (idempotent re-accept); the grant is not re-fired.

account_type.description: The account type the product access landed on.

account_id.description: The user or org id the product access landed on.

products.description: The products the invite granted access to.

grant.description: Whether the starter grant was forwarded to billing (`fired`) or deferred for a later human-gated backfill (`deferred`). Omitted on an idempotent re-accept.

409.description: The invite's state changed concurrently (a competing accept/expire/revoke won the race) — retry.

410.description: The invite is expired or revoked and can no longer be accepted.

get.description: List all active Ed25519 signing public keys. Public endpoint, no authentication required. These keys are used to verify IntegrityCertificate signatures.

instance_metadata.description: Optional: instance metadata (hostname, region, version only). No PII, API keys, or secrets allowed. Unknown fields are rejected.

post.description: Starts a claim on an MCP server you operate (identified by its endpoint URL, e.g. `https://api.example.com/mcp`) and returns the DNS TXT record to place on the server's origin domain apex (`mnemom-verification=<token>`). Idempotent per (owner, server_id): re-POSTing the same server returns the same pending token. IP-literal hosts and non-http(s) URLs are rejected. Rate-limited per user and per IP.

200.description: Claim created or idempotently re-fetched; TXT record returned.

verification.description: Everything needed to place the DNS TXT record at the origin domain apex (the domain that serves the MCP server).

host.description: Origin domain apex the record goes on.

name.description: DNS record name (apex = `@`).

get.description: Returns the caller's MCP-server claims with status, origin domain, verification time, Honor Roll opt-in, and public response note.

put.summary: Opt a verified MCP server in/out of the Honor Roll
put.description: Sets explicit, revocable Honor Roll consent for a verified MCP server. Verified claims only (409 otherwise). The `{id}` path parameter is the URL-encoded server endpoint URL.

get.summary: Public MCP-server claim status (no auth, no PII)
get.description: Credential-free, cacheable projection consumed by the isittrustready.ai MCP-readiness rubric. Always returns 200; an unknown or unverified server yields `claimed:false`. Contains ZERO PII — only `server_id`, `claimed`, `honor_roll`, and the owner-published `response_note`. `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`; `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`. The `{id}` path parameter is the URL-encoded server endpoint URL.

put.summary: Set a verified MCP server's public owner response
put.description: Publishes a plain-text owner response (≤500 chars; control and bidi/zero-width characters are stripped server-side) rendered on the public MCP-readiness report. Verified claims only (409 otherwise). An empty note clears it. The `{id}` path parameter is the URL-encoded server endpoint URL.

post.summary: Verify an MCP-server claim via DNS TXT
post.description: Looks up the origin domain apex TXT records over a fixed DoH resolver (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1) for `mnemom-verification=<token>`. Found → the claim is marked verified. Not found → `{claimed:false, reason:"txt-not-found"}` (HTTP 200; retry after DNS propagation). A successful verify by a different owner transfers control (anti-squat). The `{id}` path parameter is the URL-encoded server endpoint URL. Rate-limited per user and per IP.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The URL-encoded MCP server endpoint URL being verified.

200.description: Verification result (verified, or a friendly retryable not-found).

get.summary: Get the authenticated user's effective org-context envelope
get.description: Returns the active org context, the full membership list, and any user preferences that affect the dashboard. Per ADR-044 Piece 1 / migration 164. The dashboard's authoritative endpoint for "who am I, which org am I in, what are my memberships." `active` falls back to the most-recently-accepted multi-user org, then the personal org; `null` only if the user has zero memberships.

release_ring.description: The active org's release ring (MNE-889), resolved from plan.feature_flags.release_ring. Defaults to 'ga' (general availability) — the caller-side input to the KV release switchboard that gates feature exposure without a redeploy.

patch.summary: Set the authenticated user's active org
patch.description: Switches the user's active org via `set_user_active_org` RPC; the `active_org_id` is persisted to `user_preferences.preferences`. Body is `{ org_id: string }`. Returns the same envelope shape as `GET /me/context`. Returns 403 with `code: 'not_a_member'` if the user is not a member of the target org. Per ADR-044 Piece 1 / migration 164.

org_id.description: Org ID to switch the active context to. The user must be a member.

200.description: Active org switched. Response envelope matches GET /me/context.

post.summary: Query your own org's diagnostic log lines (self-serve)
post.description: MNE-382 (O8 supportability). Returns a STRUCTURED, ALLOWLISTED PROJECTION of the authenticated caller's OWN org's diagnostic log lines from the Tier-3 Loki mirror — operational metadata only (timestamp, level, event type, request_id, agent_id, status, duration_ms, http method, route template). The raw log body and any free-text `error` / `stack` / `message` / prompt / request-body content are never returned (GDPR data minimization). The org is resolved SERVER-SIDE from the authenticated identity and force-injected as the query scope; a caller can never name the org or supply a raw query (`org_id` / `query` / `selector` in the body → 400). Restricted to owner/admin/auditor. Fails closed: no resolvable org → 403; Loki creds unconfigured → 503.

schema.description: All fields optional. The query is always scoped to your org server-side; `org_id` / `query` / `selector` / `stream` are rejected (400).

level.description: Filter to a single severity level.

start.description: Window start (ISO-8601 or epoch-ms). Clamped to at most 7 days before `end`.

end.description: Window end (ISO-8601 or epoch-ms). Clamped to now.

limit.description: Max entries to return (default 100, capped at 500).

200.description: Allowlisted operational-metadata projection of the org's matching log lines.

org_id.description: The server-resolved org the query was scoped to.

502.description: The log backend query failed or was unreachable.

503.description: Self-serve log query is not available in this environment.

get.summary: Check the authenticated caller's own entitlement to a product
get.description: Self-service entitlement check (MNE-7401). Answers 'do I, the caller, have access to `product`' using the caller's own credential (cookie, bearer, or API key) — deliberately not admin-gated and not parameterized by accountId, so it can never become an IDOR letting one account query another's grant; it only ever resolves the grant against the authenticated caller's own identity. Added so mnemom-research-grade's own OIDC callback (which is reachable without going through this repo's `/v1/auth/oidc/finalize`) can check entitlement before minting its session.

parameters.name: product
parameters.description: Which product's entitlement to check.

502.description: The entitlement lookup failed (fails closed — never reads as access granted).

get.summary: Read the caller's org mu-engine budgets
get.description: Returns the mu budgets configured for the authenticated caller's organization, optionally with month-to-date spend (`status=true`, which answers `{statuses:[{budget, spentMmu, pctOfSoft, crossedThresholds}]}` — the input a burn-down meter needs). Same org-context + RBAC resolution as `GET /billing/mu` (any org member may read). api forwards to the mnemom-mu upstream `GET /v1/budgets?account={accountId}` with the server-resolved account id; a client-supplied `account` parameter is overwritten, never trusted.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Target org id. Defaults to the caller's primary org. A non-member is denied 403.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: When `true`, return budget STATUS (month-to-date spend + percent of soft cap + crossed alert thresholds) instead of the bare budget rows.

200.description: mu budgets for the org (mnemom-mu response, verbatim).

post.summary: Mint a Stripe Customer Session for the caller's org (saved-method redisplay)
post.description: Mints a short-lived Stripe Customer Session client secret for the authenticated caller's organization. Passed into `stripe.elements()` as `customerSessionClientSecret`, it lets the Payment Element redisplay the org's saved payment methods and offer the save-for-future checkbox — the modern returning-buyer flow. Creates a Stripe object only: no charge, no ledger movement. Owner/admin only, same org resolution as the purchase route. Takes NO request body — any body sent is ignored; api authors the upstream request entirely from the server-resolved `billing_account_id`. The secret expires roughly 30 minutes after minting, so request a fresh one per Payment Element mount. Response is mnemom-billing's verbatim `{stripeCustomerId, customerSessionClientSecret}` on 201.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Target org id. Defaults to the caller's primary org. A non-member is denied 403.

201.description: Customer Session created (mnemom-billing response, verbatim): `{stripeCustomerId, customerSessionClientSecret}`.

post.summary: Set or remove one org member's monthly mu spending limit
post.description: Allocates spend authority out of the org's shared mu pool by setting ONE member's monthly hard cap (a `user`-scoped budget row), or removes it. This is how an org admin 'distributes' mu to their team: mu is a closed-loop instrument that is neither cash-redeemable nor transferable between accounts, and there is no member-level ledger account — one org, one balance — so per-member control is a cap, never a balance move. Owner/admin of the target org only; every other role, and any caller who is not a member of `org_id`, is denied 403. `org_id` is REQUIRED (no primary-org fallback: a write must never land on a different tenant than the admin is looking at). api resolves the org's `billing_account_id` server-side from the proven membership and authors the upstream `POST /v1/budgets` body itself; client-supplied `account`, `accountId`, `actor`, `cell`, `scopeType`, `scopeRef` or soft-cap fields are rejected 400 rather than ignored. The `userId` being capped must itself be a member of the same org (else 404). Presents api's budget-scoped identity (`MU_BUDGET_SERVICE_TOKEN`), never the grant-capable admin token; unset ⇒ 503 fail-closed.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Target org id. REQUIRED — a mu write never falls back to the caller's primary org. A non-member, or a member outside owner/admin, is denied 403.

userId.description: The org member whose limit is being set. Must be a member of `org_id`.

hardCapMmuPerMonth.description: Monthly hard cap in millimu as a whole-number string (billing casts it to bigint, so it is not sent as a JSON number). `"0"` is a real setting — this member may spend nothing this month — and is deliberately distinct from `null`, which REMOVES the limit. The field is required: a missing field is a 400, never a silent removal.

200.description: Limit set or removed. `{budget: <mnemom-billing Budget row>}`.

post.summary: Create a Stripe PaymentIntent to buy mu by dollar amount at the peg
post.description: Creates a Stripe PaymentIntent for the authenticated caller's organization to buy mu at the fixed peg (1 mu = 1¢, face-only retail — MNE-3255). Owner/admin only (`org_id` query targets a specific org; a non-member or under-privileged caller is denied 403). api resolves the org's `billing_account_id` server-side and authors the upstream body itself — a client-supplied account reference is never forwarded. `amountUsdCents` must be a JSON integer; the min/max purchase bounds are enforced by mnemom-billing (its 400 passes back verbatim). `idempotencyKey` is REQUIRED — billing scopes the Stripe idempotency key to it so a retry of the same purchase cannot double-charge. Response is mnemom-billing's verbatim `{paymentIntentId, clientSecret, expectedMmu}` on 201; `expectedMmu` is a display prediction, never mint authority — the ledger credits only when `payment_intent.succeeded` arrives on the webhook.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Target org id. Defaults to the caller's primary org. A non-member is denied 403.

amountUsdCents.description: Whole USD cents to charge. Bounds are enforced by mnemom-billing (MIN/MAX_PURCHASE_CENTS), not mirrored here.

idempotencyKey.description: Caller-chosen retry key. billing composes the Stripe idempotency key from it, so re-submitting with the same key cannot double-charge.

201.description: PaymentIntent created (mnemom-billing response, verbatim): `{paymentIntentId, clientSecret, expectedMmu}`.

post.summary: Create a Stripe SetupIntent to capture a card for the caller's org
post.description: Creates a Stripe SetupIntent (card capture, no charge) for the authenticated caller's organization — the deliberate second ask of Pricing Model v2 (MNE-3255): sign-up needs no card, and capturing one triggers the one-time intro grant when `setup_intent.succeeded` arrives on the webhook (never on this call). Owner/admin only, same org resolution as the purchase route. Takes NO request body — any body sent is ignored; api authors the upstream request entirely from the server-resolved `billing_account_id`. Response is mnemom-billing's verbatim `{stripeCustomerId, setupIntentId, clientSecret}` on 201.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Target org id. Defaults to the caller's primary org. A non-member is denied 403.

201.description: SetupIntent created (mnemom-billing response, verbatim): `{stripeCustomerId, setupIntentId, clientSecret}`.

post.summary: Stripe webhook for mu top-up grants (signature-authenticated upstream)
post.description: Stripe → api → mnemom-mu grant path (MNE-2516). Accepts Stripe webhook deliveries (e.g. `payment_intent.succeeded`) and forwards them BYTE-VERBATIM to the ledger's `/v1/stripe/webhook` consumer, which verifies the `stripe-signature` header against its webhook secret and fail-closes (401 bad signature, 503 unconfigured). api adds no authentication of its own — the payload, not the transport, is what is authenticated — and no ledger logic. Purchase grants land exactly-once with Stripe provenance; retail grant creation happens ONLY through this path.

200.description: Ledger webhook consumer result, passed through verbatim.

401.description: Ledger consumer rejected the signature. Body is mnemom-mu's VERBATIM error shape (e.g. `{"error":"bad_signature"}`), NOT an api error envelope.

503.description: Ledger consumer is unconfigured (no webhook secret). Body is mnemom-mu's VERBATIM error shape, NOT an api error envelope.

get.description: Returns the current aggregated `network_campaign_state` grouped by axis (substrate / vertical / pattern / source), plus per-state totals. Backs the customer-facing L4 thermometer page. Public-aggregate disclosure: any authenticated principal may read; rows carry no per-tenant identifiers (L0 fingerprints only).

parameters.name: max_buckets
parameters.description: Top-N most elevated buckets returned per axis. Clamped to [1, 50]; default 10.

get.summary: OAuth 2.1 authorization endpoint (renders the consent screen)
get.description: Begins the authorization-code + PKCE flow. Identity is delegated to Supabase GoTrue via the Mnemom session cookie; an unauthenticated user is redirected to the hosted login and returns here. With a valid session, renders the server-side consent screen listing the requested scopes in product language. PKCE S256 is mandatory; redirect_uri must exactly match one registered for the client.

302.description: Redirect to the hosted login (unauthenticated) or back to the client's redirect_uri with an error per RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1.

400.description: Unknown client_id or unregistered redirect_uri — rendered as an HTML error page; never redirected (open-redirect guard).

post.summary: Submit the OAuth consent decision (Allow / Deny)
post.description: Processes the consent form. On Allow, mints a single-use, 60-second authorization code bound to the client, the exact redirect_uri, and the PKCE challenge, then redirects back to the client with code + state. On Deny, redirects with error=access_denied. CSRF-protected (SameSite=Lax cookie + signed token); the acting org is bound here and is immutable for tokens minted from the code.

302.description: Redirect back to the client with code+state, or with an OAuth error.

get.description: Server-rendered approval page a human opens (from verification_uri / verification_uri_complete) to authorize a device. Unauthenticated users are redirected to the hosted login and returned here. Leads with the user_code so the human confirms it matches their device before an explicit Approve (RFC 8628 §5.4). Same origin as the AS so the session cookie + CSRF apply.

200.description: The approval page (HTML), or a terminal result page (invalid/expired code).

302.description: Redirect to the hosted login (unauthenticated), returning here after sign-in.

404.description: No live device code for that user_code (HTML).

post.summary: Submit the device approval decision (Approve / Deny)
post.description: Processes the device verification form. On Approve, binds the device code to the authenticated user and the chosen org (default: the user's personal org) — the claim-first ownership moment — so the polling client can then exchange it for tokens. On Deny, marks the code denied. CSRF-protected (signed token bound to user + client + user_code); session must still be valid.

200.description: Terminal result page — authorized, denied, or code-not-found (HTML).

404.description: No live device code for that user_code (HTML).

409.description: The code expired or was already used before approval committed (HTML).

post.description: Begins the device authorization grant for headless agents / CLIs that cannot perform an interactive redirect. Returns a device_code (the polled secret), a short human-typed user_code, and verification URIs. Public-client posture; the device_code itself is the proof-of-possession (PKCE is not required). The user approves at verification_uri; the client then polls /oauth/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code.

get.summary: List an org's active OAuth grants (connected apps / sessions)
get.description: Lists the live OAuth grants (unrevoked, refresh-token-unexpired) issued against an org — the owner-facing 'Connected apps / active sessions' view. Returns only non-secret metadata: client, scopes (including per-agent resource scopes), issued/expiry times, and a best-effort last-used stamp — never any token material or hash. Caller must be an owner or admin of `org_id`. Optionally filter to grants connected to a specific agent with `agent_id`.

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: Keep only grants carrying a resource scope (MNE-796) for this agent.

items.description: A live OAuth grant (active session / connected app). Carries only non-secret metadata — never any token material or hash.

grant_id.description: Opaque grant id; address it in POST /oauth/grants/revoke.

org_id.description: The org the grant acts within (immutable post-issuance).

last_used_at.description: Best-effort last-seen stamp; null if not yet observed.

get.summary: OAuth grant-lifecycle audit trail for an org
get.description: Lists the governance audit entries for the OAuth grant lifecycle (consent granted, consent denied, owner revocation) scoped to the owner's org, so revocation and consent are accountable. Caller must be an owner or admin of `org_id`. Carries no token material.

post.summary: Owner-initiated revocation of an OAuth grant by id
post.description: Revokes a grant the caller owns, by its opaque `grant_id`, within an org the caller owns/admins. Distinct from RFC 7009 POST /oauth/revoke (which lets a token HOLDER revoke its OWN token). Idempotent: revoking an already-revoked grant in the caller's org returns revoked:true with already_revoked:true. The revocation cascades to the grant's refresh token (a single grant row holds both the access and refresh token hashes), and is recorded on the org's audit trail (action=oauth.grant_revoked). A grant in another org — or unknown — returns 404 with no distinction (no cross-org existence oracle).

already_revoked.description: true when the grant was already revoked before this call.

post.description: Returns the activeness + metadata of an access token per RFC 7662. The caller MUST authenticate: because Mnemom's OAuth clients are public (no client secret), there is no client-credentials path, so the caller authenticates as a USER (bearer / api-key / cookie). active:true with full metadata is returned ONLY when the token is live AND the authenticated caller owns/admins the token's org; otherwise the response is {active:false} with no other fields — the endpoint is never a token existence/validity oracle for tokens the caller does not control. Only opaque access tokens (mcp_at_) are introspectable; refresh tokens and unknown values report active:false.

Registers a public OAuth client for the MCP flow. No client secret is issued (PKCE-protected public clients only). redirect_uris must be HTTPS, or an RFC 8252 loopback (http://127.0.0.1[:port]/..., http://[::1][:port]/..., or http://localhost[:port]/...), and are exact-matched at /authorize. Registration is abuse-guarded with per-IP and global daily caps.

grant_types.description: Requested grant types. A client requesting ONLY urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code (RFC 8628 device flow) may omit redirect_uris; any authorization_code client must supply at least one redirect_uri.

post.description: Revokes the presented access or refresh token. Returns 200 even for an unknown token, per RFC 7009 §2.2.

Exchanges an authorization code (+ PKCE code_verifier) for a short-lived opaque access token and a rotating refresh token, or rotates a refresh token. Authorization codes are single-use; refresh tokens are single-use (rotated on every exchange). Public-client posture: no client authentication (token_endpoint_auth_method=none).

400.description: OAuth error (invalid_request / invalid_grant / unsupported_grant_type / authorization_pending / slow_down / expired_token / access_denied).

get.description: Retrieve the history of on-chain Merkle root anchoring events. Returns a paginated list of all anchors with their transaction details, included agents, and verification status.

parameters.name: chain
parameters.description: Filter by blockchain network (matches on_chain_anchors.chain CHECK constraint)

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: Filter anchors that include this agent

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of time range

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of time range

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return (handler default 50; values above 100 are clamped to 100).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of records to skip for pagination

200.description: On-chain anchoring history: the page of anchor rows plus the effective `limit`/`offset` echoed back by the handler (handleGetAnchoringHistory in src/on-chain/handlers.ts).

limit.description: Effective page size applied to this response.

offset.description: Effective offset applied to this response.

get.description: Get the current on-chain anchoring status for an agent. Returns the most recent anchor, pending publications, and overall on-chain coverage statistics.

200.description: On-chain status for the agent, as assembled by the get_on_chain_status RPC (migrations 057/058): the agent's latest score publication, the latest confirmed anchor, and the agent's current Merkle-tree summary. Each of the three nested objects is `null` when no matching row exists.

latest_score_publication.description: The agent's most recent row in score_publications, or `null` when the agent has never been published.

latest_anchor.description: The most recent `confirmed` on-chain anchor, or `null` when none is confirmed yet. (The RPC filters to status='confirmed' and omits gas_used/created_at.)

merkle_tree.description: Summary of the agent's current Merkle tree (from agent_merkle_trees), or `null` when the agent has no tree.

get.description:
Verify an agent's Merkle commitment. The agent's stored root is **recomputed from its stored leaf hashes**, the stored `leaf_count` is checked against the actual number of leaves, and — when `leaf_index` is supplied — a real inclusion proof for that leaf is generated and verified against the recomputed root and returned so the caller can re-derive it independently. The confirming anchor is then looked up by the **recomputed** root, so an anchor row can never vouch for a root nobody can rebuild.

**Scope limit, stated rather than hidden:** the anchored root is read from Mnemom's own anchor record, not from a Base RPC call. A `verified: true` therefore means "this tree is internally consistent and matches the root we recorded as anchored" — it does not by itself prove the chain agrees. `verification.anchored_root_source` reports this.

parameters.name: leaf_index
parameters.description: Optional. Zero-based index of a single leaf to prove inclusion for. When supplied, the response carries an `inclusion_proof` (leaf hash + sibling path) that has been verified against the recomputed root; the caller can replay it without trusting this endpoint. When omitted, only the root recomputation and leaf-count checks are performed.

200.description: Proof verification result. `verified: true` requires ALL of: the root recomputes from the stored leaf hashes, `leaf_count` agrees with the leaf array, any requested inclusion proof verifies, and a `confirmed` anchor exists for the recomputed root. Any failed step returns `verified: false` with a `reason` — never a bare true. (handleVerifyProof in src/on-chain/handlers.ts.)

verified.description: True only when the agent's root was successfully recomputed from its stored leaves AND a confirmed on-chain anchor exists for that recomputed root (and, if `leaf_index` was supplied, its inclusion proof verified).

reason.description: Present only when `verified` is false. `no_merkle_tree`: the agent has no merkle tree row; `no_checkpoint`: the tree has no merkle_root yet; `no_leaf_hashes`: a root is stored but no leaves are, so it cannot be rebuilt; `root_mismatch`: the root recomputed from the stored leaves does not equal the stored root (tampering or corruption); `leaf_count_mismatch`: the stored leaf_count disagrees with the number of stored leaves (silent truncation); `leaf_index_out_of_range`: the requested leaf_index exceeds the tree; `inclusion_proof_failed`: the proof for the requested leaf does not reconstruct the root; `not_anchored`: the tree verifies but has no confirmed anchor.

merkle_root.description: The agent's stored Merkle root. Present when a checkpoint exists (i.e. absent for the `no_merkle_tree`/`no_checkpoint` cases).

recomputed_root.description: The root recomputed from the stored leaf hashes. Returned only on `root_mismatch`, so the discrepancy is inspectable.

leaf_count.description: Leaf count, included on the `leaf_count_mismatch` and `leaf_index_out_of_range` failures for diagnosis.

leaf_hashes_length.description: Actual number of stored leaf hashes. Returned only on `leaf_count_mismatch`.

inclusion_proof.description: The verified inclusion proof for the requested leaf. Null when `leaf_index` was not supplied. The caller can recompute the root from `leaf_hash` plus the sibling path without trusting this endpoint.

verification.description: What was actually checked, so a caller never has to infer it from `verified` alone.

root_recomputed_from_leaves.description: True when the stored root was successfully rebuilt from the stored leaves.

leaf_count_checked.description: Whether the stored `leaf_count` was available to compare against the leaf array. False when the row carries no usable count, in which case the silent-truncation check could not run — reported rather than skipped silently.

inclusion_proof_verified.description: True when a requested inclusion proof verified; null when no `leaf_index` was supplied (not checked, as distinct from checked-and-failed).

anchored_root_source.description: Where the anchored root was read from. `mnemom_database` means Mnemom's own anchor record, NOT a Base RPC read — the residual trust assumption, disclosed rather than hidden. Null when no confirmed anchor was found.

anchor.description: The confirming anchor. Present only when `verified` is true.

post.summary: Generate guidance for an onboarding checklist step.
post.description: MNE-5508: Accepts a checklist item ID and user context; generates LLM-driven guidance narration and a bounded action suggestion. Gated behind `ONBOARDING_GUIDE_ENABLED` (dark by default) and `ONBOARDING_GUIDE_ALLOWLIST` (defaults to @mnemom.ai). Requires authentication.

checklist_item_id.description: The ID of the onboarding checklist item (e.g., 'org.create', 'agent.alignment-card').

facts.description: Optional contextual facts about the user's state (e.g., org_exists: true, first_agent_chosen: false).

completed_steps.description: Optional array of checklist item IDs the user has already completed.

user_goal.description: Optional user-provided goal or context (e.g., 'Build a support bot', 'Set up trusted governance').

org_id.description: Optional organization ID for multi-tenant context.

user_id.description: Optional user ID (can be overridden from auth context).

200.description: Guidance generated successfully. Returns narration, suggested action, next step, and session correlation ID.

narration.description: The LLM-generated guidance narration for this step.

A non-owner receives 403 before any billing state is read — Stripe-customer existence is never disclosed to unauthorized roles.

Gated behind the `ORG_SELF_SERVE_RESTORE_ENABLED` flag; 404s (as if the route doesn't exist) when that flag is off.

post.summary: Replay a webhook event to its eligible endpoints
post.description: Re-dispatches a previously recorded webhook event to all org endpoints subscribed to its event_type (or to the explicit subset supplied in the request body). Requires the `webhook_notifications` feature flag and owner/admin role on the target org. Cross-tenant access returns 404. Replay is idempotent on the `Idempotency-Key` header; a replayed key with a different body returns 422 and a conflicting in-flight key returns 409. When no endpoints are eligible the response is 200 with an empty `deliveries` array; when at least one delivery is enqueued the response is 201 with delivery descriptors (and an optional `failed_endpoints` list for endpoints that could not be enqueued).

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the webhook event to replay. Must belong to the path org_id; cross-tenant lookups return 404.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-supplied key that makes replay idempotent. Re-sending the same key with the same body returns the original result; re-sending with a different body returns 422; a conflicting in-flight key returns 409.

endpoint_ids.description: Optional explicit subset of endpoint ids to replay to. Endpoints not subscribed to the event's type are silently skipped. When omitted, all eligible endpoints are targeted.

200.description: No eligible endpoints — nothing was enqueued. Returned when the event has no subscribers (or the supplied `endpoint_ids` subset matches none).

201.description: One or more deliveries were enqueued for replay.

failed_endpoints.description: Endpoints that matched the event but could not be enqueued (e.g. transient infrastructure error). Each entry names the endpoint and the reason.

get.description:
Opens a Server-Sent Events stream that emits webhook events delivered to the org in near-real-time. Requires the `webhook_notifications` feature flag and owner/admin role on the target org. The cursor is resolved from the `since` query parameter, falling back to the `Last-Event-ID` header when `since` is absent — clients reconnecting after a drop should send the last event id they observed. The stream caps at 5 minutes per connection, polls the underlying queue every 1 second, and emits a keepalive comment every 15 seconds. Frame types emitted on the stream:

- `ready` — sent immediately after the stream opens, carries the resolved cursor.
- `webhook.event` — one frame per webhook event, payload mirrors the event record.
- keepalive — SSE comment line (`:keepalive`) every 15s to keep intermediaries from idling the connection.
- `close` — sent when the 5-minute cap is reached, before the server closes the socket.
- `error` — sent on unrecoverable stream errors before the socket closes.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Cursor (event id) to resume from. When omitted, the server falls back to the `Last-Event-ID` request header; when neither is supplied, the stream starts at the current tail.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Standard SSE reconnection header. Used as the cursor when the `since` query parameter is not supplied.

200.description: Server-Sent Events stream of webhook events. The connection is capped at 5 minutes; clients should reconnect and resume via `Last-Event-ID` or `since`.

Cache-Control.description: Disables intermediary caching of the stream.

X-Accel-Buffering.description: Disables proxy response buffering (nginx-family) so frames flush immediately.

Connection.description: Keeps the underlying TCP connection open for the duration of the stream.

schema.description: Sequence of SSE frames. Each non-keepalive frame has an `event:` line naming the frame type (`ready`, `webhook.event`, `close`, `error`), an `id:` line carrying the event cursor (for `webhook.event` frames), and a `data:` line containing a JSON payload. Keepalive frames are SSE comments (`:keepalive`).

post.summary: Accept a presentation invite (attach the grant to the caller).
post.description: The endpoint the invite email's CTA lands at after the recipient signs in / signs up. The single-use token comes from the body `{token}` or the `?token=` query param; it's hashed and matched to a pending grant for THIS presentation. On success the grant is attached to the caller (user_id + accepted_at set, token consumed) and the caller's tier is returned. The invite email is address-specific: the caller's account email MUST match the grant email (case-insensitive) or a 403 is returned. Authed user. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. MNE-1428.

parameters.description: The presentation slug.

post.summary: Send a governed turn to the presentation's agent (Aletheia).
post.description: One governed Aletheia turn (MNE-1428): routed through the Mnemom gateway (Safe House / AIP / CLPI / back-door screen in-path), executing read-only Mnemom MCP tools + a curated readiness brief scoped to the viewer's grant tier. Returns her answer, the per-round verdict cascade ({cfd,aip,policy,cbd}), citations, and a compact attestation. Authed user; requires an ACTIVE grant for the presentation. A Safe House hard-block is a governance success, not an error: it returns 200 with `blocked:true` and no answer. Chat is intentionally NOT idempotent (each turn is new), so no Idempotency-Key is required.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The presentation slug.

deck.description: The deck's own text, handed over by the page that is already rendering it, so Aletheia reads it as her primary source. Capped server-side.

history.description: Optional prior turns for multi-turn context. Only {role:'user'|'assistant', content:string} entries are honored; the newest 20 are kept.

200.description: The turn's result. `ok:false` with `blocked:true` means Safe House withheld the response (governance success).

502.description: The governed chat runtime is currently unavailable.

503.description: Presentation chat is not configured on this deployment.

post.summary: Start an Aletheia voice session for the presentation.
post.description: Opens a voice session for the presentation's agent (Aletheia, MNE-1428 voice). Creates a Retell web call, mints a short-lived scoped voice-grant token, and hands it plus the deck + scope to the separate voice backend, which then proxies each spoken turn to `POST /v1/presentations/{slug}/chat` bearing that token. Governance (Safe House / tier / tools) stays entirely in the chat runtime — this endpoint re-implements none of it, and the token is authentication-only (the active grant remains the sole authority). Authed user; requires an ACTIVE grant. Returns the Retell web-call access token + call id for the browser SDK. Not idempotent (each session is new), so no Idempotency-Key is required.

parameters.description: The presentation slug.

get.description: Returns the agent-scope protection spec as authored. Response is content-negotiated — YAML by default, or JSON with `Accept: application/json`. Pass `?include_composition=true` to include the `_composition` metadata block describing which scopes were merged. Pass `?include=sources` (see ADR-053) for the scope-resolution envelope — the contributing layers plus the composed result; the envelope shape is scope-specific (the four-scope `{teams[], agent}` body is the agent variant consumed by the dashboard editor). ETag is computed from `content_hash` (cards-as-primitive Phase 1); `If-None-Match` returns 304. For the composed view across scopes, use the `/effective` sub-resource (Wave 2).

parameters.name: include_composition
parameters.description: Include the `_composition` metadata block on the response body.

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: Response format. YAML is canonical; JSON is returned only on explicit `application/json`. The `?include=sources` envelope is JSON-only.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: When `sources`, returns the four-scope envelope `{platform, org, teams[], agent, composed, composed_stale, my_role}` (see ADR-053). The envelope is JSON-only.

ETag.description: `"sha256:<hex>"` of the canonical body. Stable across reads; changes on PUT.

X-Card-Version.description: Monotonic version counter (cards-as-primitive Phase 1).

304.description: Not Modified — the client's `If-None-Match` matches the current ETag.

put.summary: Publish or replace the protection manifest
put.description: Accepts YAML (`text/yaml`, `application/yaml`) or JSON. Body is the full `UnifiedProtectionCard`; server-side composition merges it across the platform → org → team → agent cascade and writes the canonical composed card. Requires `Idempotency-Key`. Honors an optional `If-Match` for optimistic concurrency (stale → 412). Body cap 128 KiB. See ADR-008 and ADR-023.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-supplied idempotency token. Replays within 24 hours return the stored result. See ADR-023.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency token. Pass the `ETag` from a recent `GET` (`"sha256:<hex64>"` shape) to make the write conditional: a stale ETag returns `412 Precondition Failed`, a malformed one `400`. Omit it to publish unconditionally.

200.description: Composed canonical card after the write.

ETag.description: `"sha256:<hex>"` of the new canonical body.

X-Card-Version.description: Bumped monotonically on every PUT that changes content_hash.

get.description: Returns the composed canonical protection card (platform → org → team → agent cascade applied) with `_composition.field_provenance` always populated. The provenance map carries per-key `{layer, layer_id?, kind?}` entries showing which authoring scope contributed each leaf. Caller-aware redaction: layer labels (`platform` / `org` / `team` / `agent` / `derived`) are always visible; `layer_id` is only revealed to callers who can read that scope. cards-as-primitive Phase 4 W2.2.

ETag.description: `"sha256:<hex>"` of the composed body.

X-Card-Version.description: Monotonic version counter.

post.summary: Explain policy evaluation for the protection card
post.description:
Calls the policy engine in dry-run mode against the agent's composed protection card and returns a structured trace + care-framed remediations. Optional `enrich: true` runs an LLM pass over the structured remediations to produce long-form prose; off by default. Read-style POST — no state mutation, no Idempotency-Key.

This endpoint returns a deferred Phase-5 stub (`trace: null`) — the dedicated protection evaluator has not landed, so no policy evaluation runs and no request field is required. `request_snippet.tool_name` is accepted and ignored today; when the evaluator lands it becomes REQUIRED with a **400** `missing_tool_name`, as on the alignment explain (MNE-5820).

turn_id.description: Optional — bind to a specific gateway turn.

request_snippet.description: The tool call to explain. Optional and currently ignored — this endpoint returns a Phase-5 stub before any evaluation runs. Becomes required when the protection evaluator lands (MNE-5820).

tool_name.description: A TOOL IDENTIFIER — the name a runtime invokes (`Read`, `Grep`, `Bash`), matched against `capabilities.<name>.tools[]`. NOT a card action (`code_read`, `inference`, `tool_use`); those live in `autonomy.bounded_actions` and never match here.

enrich.description: When true, runs an LLM pass over the structured remediations. Off by default.

trace.description: EvaluationResult from @mnemom/policy-engine. Null for protection in V1.

enriched.description: True when the LLM enrichment ran.

post.summary: Reveal the decrypted withheld content of a review-hold
post.description: Return the decrypted original held message of a Safe House review-hold so an authorized human can read it before ruling (Wave 4). POST (not GET) so the `SameSite=Lax` session cookie makes it CSRF-safe like `/resolve`; the request carries no body. Customer/human auth (an authenticated member of the org that governs the review's agent, or platform staff). A `review_id` outside the caller's authority returns **404, never 403** (no existence leak, mirroring resolve). The decrypt happens gateway-side (keys never leave the gateway) and is strictly read-only — it never changes the hold's state. The plaintext is disclosed only after its reveal is durably audit-logged. Works for a hold in any status. Fails closed (**502**) on a gateway/vault error or an audit-write failure — never a fabricated or unaudited plaintext.

The human decider for a Safe House review-hold (Wave 4). Customer/human auth (an authenticated org member, or platform staff) — the resolver is ALWAYS the authenticated principal, NEVER read from the body. A `review_id` outside the caller's org fleet returns **404, never 403** (no existence leak). `allow`/`deny` finalize the hold through the gateway (a NEW Ed25519-signed decision row; on `allow`, the decrypted original plus a single-use, content-bound allow-token are returned). `escalate` is **non-terminal**: it records the action, signals higher-tier attention, and leaves the hold `pending`. When the agent's card requires dual-control, a terminal ruling needs **two distinct** resolvers to concur — a same-identity second action returns **409**, and divergent votes escalate.

decision.description: `allow`/`deny` finalize (single-control) or count toward dual-control concurrence; `escalate` is non-terminal.

reason.description: Optional free-text rationale recorded on the approvals ledger.

200.description: The resolution outcome. Terminal on a finalized `allow`/`deny` (with the allow-token + decrypted content on `allow`); otherwise `pending` (escalated, or awaiting a second dual-control approver).

allow_token.description: Single-use, `content_hash`-bound, short-TTL token honored by the gateway on re-submit. Present only on a finalized `allow`.

content.description: The decrypted original held content. Present only on a finalized `allow`.

awaiting.description: Present when dual-control is required and this is the first concurring resolver.

escalated.description: True when the action escalated the hold for higher-tier attention (explicit escalate, or divergent dual-control votes).

post.summary: Force-end every active sim session for an agent (runaway recovery).
post.description: DB-authoritative, Durable-Object-independent recovery for a stuck/runaway Dojo session: aborts every non-terminal (`pending`/`running`/`paused`) `dojo_sim_sessions` row for the agent directly in the control plane, clearing the one-active-session-per-agent lock even when the per-session runner DO has crashed or been evicted (the ghost-DO case `/sim/{session_id}/stop` cannot resolve, because that path no-ops the DB when the DO has no in-memory state). Keyed by `agent_id` because a locked-out caller holds the agent id, not the orphaned session id. Idempotent: returns `{ ok: true, ended: 0 }` when nothing was active. MNE-531.

200.description: Active sessions aborted (or none were active).

post.summary: Create a Dojo sim session and begin the runner ("Begin Sim").
post.description:
Creates a `dojo_sim_sessions` row for the agent + scenario and starts the server-side runner (a per-session Durable Object that drives the Agent Smith ↔ agent loop and survives the human closing the tab). The runner resolves the agent's gateway compute key server-side BY `agent_id` (via the agent↔TryMeConfig link from onboarding) — the cleartext key never travels in the request. Emits SimEvents readable via `GET /v1/sim/{session_id}/stream`. MNE-531.

This operation returns `409` for THREE distinct causes; branch on the stable `error.code`, NEVER on the status alone (a client that assumes 409 means "a session is already running" will offer a force-end remedy that cannot help, succeeds at ending nothing, and loops):

- `active_sim_session` — the agent already has a `pending`/`running`/`paused` session. `error.details.session_id` carries the BLOCKING session's id so the client can stop that session directly. It is omitted (no `details` at all) on the DB unique-constraint backstop path, where a concurrent create raced the pre-check and the racing session's id is not known.
- `dojo_provider_key_missing` — no dojo provider key resolves for the agent's provider. An admin must set it (`/admin/dojo`) and the agent must be bound to its Try-Me config. Force-ending sessions does nothing for this.
- `agent_unnamed` — `agents.name` is empty for this agent, and the sim needs a name to spar as it. Remedy: `PUT /v1/agents/{id}` with `{"name": "…"}` (2-32 chars, letters/digits/hyphens), then retry. Names are normally written at birth from the gateway's `x-mnemom-agent` header, but birth is NOT the only writer — do not send the operator back through birth for an agent that already exists. Force-ending sessions does nothing for this.

An unrecognised or absent code on a 409 should fall back to displaying `error.message` verbatim rather than assuming any of the above.

'builtin_opus' (default) resolves synchronously; 'human' routes a hold to the human-tier resolve endpoint. Assigns the sim agent to the corresponding STANDING, non-weakenable team-scope review-policy team before the run starts — this is owner-authoritative policy, never a per-agent card upsert the agent could weaken.

get.summary: Consistency proof that the log grew by append only.
get.description:
Returns an RFC 6962 / RFC 9162 §2.1.4 consistency proof that the tree of size `second` contains the tree of size `first` as a prefix — i.e. the first `first` entries were not reordered, altered, or removed. `second` defaults to the log's current size.

This is the only endpoint that can distinguish "the log grew" from "the log was rewritten and re-signed": an inclusion proof verifies against whatever root it is given, so it cannot detect a wholesale reissue. Chain these proofs across successive signed roots from `GET /v1/transparency/root` and the append-only claim becomes checkable rather than promised.

What it does NOT prove: that Mnemom published every root it computed. A consistent chain of roots shown to you could coexist with a different, internally-consistent chain shown to somebody else (a "split view"). Detecting that requires gossip between independent monitors. MNE-6384.

parameters.name: first
parameters.description: The earlier tree_size — typically one you already hold a signed root for.

parameters.name: second
parameters.description: The later tree_size. Defaults to the log's current size. Must be >= `first`; a request where it is smaller is rejected rather than answered, because a shrinking log is itself the finding.

200.description: Consistency proof between the two tree sizes.

construction.description: Named construction the proof is built against. Versioned wire string — a new construction mints a new identity rather than editing this one, so a verifier can never silently apply the wrong rules.

first_root.description: Merkle root at tree_size = first. Compare this against the signed root you already hold for that size — if it differs, the log was rewritten.

hashes.description: RFC 6962 §2.1.2 consistency path, in the order the §2.1.4.2 verification algorithm consumes it. Empty ONLY when first === second (nothing was appended). Note that when `first` is an exact power of two the generator omits MTH(D[0:first]) because the verifier re-derives it from first_root.

404.description: The log is empty, or one of the requested sizes exceeds the log's current size. The latter is worth investigating: if you hold a signed root for a larger size than the log now reports, the log shrank.

get.description: Returns the transparency-log row whose `composed_at` is the greatest at-or-before the `at` query parameter, plus a freshly-computed Merkle inclusion proof. `card_kind` defaults to `alignment`. cards-as-primitive Phase 5 A2.

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp.

parameters.name: card_kind
parameters.description: Defaults to `alignment`.

signed_attestation.description: JWS Compact serialization signed by Mnemom over the canonical identity tuple.

get.summary: Recent transparency-log entries for an agent.
get.description: Returns the last N transparency-log entries for the agent, newest first (`log_index.desc`), each with a freshly-computed Merkle inclusion proof. Public + unauthenticated like its siblings; the per-agent filter is the leak defense (data scoping, not org authz). Bounded by a server-clamped `limit` (default 10, max 100). `card_kind` defaults to `alignment`. An agent with no attestations returns `200 { data: [] }`. cards-as-primitive Phase 5 A2.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max entries to return; clamped server-side to 100.

parameters.name: card_kind
parameters.description: Defaults to `alignment`.

200.description: Recent log entries + inclusion proofs (newest first).

signed_attestation.description: JWS Compact serialization signed by Mnemom over the canonical identity tuple.

get.summary: Direct log entry by index, with Merkle inclusion proof.
get.description: Returns the row at `log_index` (if it belongs to `agent_id`) plus a freshly-computed inclusion proof. cards-as-primitive Phase 5 A2.

signed_attestation.description: JWS Compact serialization signed by Mnemom over the canonical identity tuple.

get.summary: Signed current Merkle root for the canonical-card transparency log.
get.description: Returns the current root + tree_size + published_at, signed by the active AAP signing key. Distinct `typ` from per-card attestations (`AAP-TransparencyRoot/v1`). Cacheable for 30 seconds; consumers refresh when they want a fresh root. cards-as-primitive Phase 5 A2.

200.description: Signed root, or an empty-state payload when the log has no entries.

typ.description: Domain separator distinguishing a signed root from a per-card attestation.

signature.description: Base64url Ed25519 signature over canonical_json(commitment), where commitment is this object MINUS `signature` — i.e. {typ, tree_size, root_hash, published_at, signing_key_id}. Verify by dropping `signature`, canonicalising the rest (sorted keys, no whitespace), and checking against the JWKS key for signing_key_id.

get.description: Returns the published advisories sorted by `published_at` desc. No authentication required — the surface is public trust messaging. Pagination via `limit` (default 20, max 100) and `offset`.

slug.description: URL-safe slug used as the customer-facing detail path.

get.summary: Fetch a published advisory by slug
get.description: Returns the canonical advisory record for `{slug}`. Drafts and archived rows are not exposed on this surface — the CMS admin endpoints serve those.

slug.description: URL-safe slug used as the customer-facing detail path.

get.description: Public IoC feed returned as a STIX 2.1 Bundle. Per-indicator SDOs carry a Mnemom `extensions` block with internal type/TLP labelling. Rate-limited at the gateway and best-effort in-handler (1 req/min/IP). Pagination via `after=<ISO8601>` (resume from the last seen `last_seen_at`).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Cursor — ISO-8601 timestamp; rows with `last_seen_at < after` are returned.

200.description: STIX 2.1 Bundle (possibly empty at GA — see calm-at-GA contract).

objects.description: STIX 2.1 indicator SDOs. Each carries a Mnemom extension with the internal indicator type + TLP + linkage to a related advisory.

next_after.description: Mnemom-extension pagination cursor. Present iff the response was capped at `limit`. Pass as `?after=` to fetch the next page.

post.description: Verify an IntegrityCertificate. Performs Ed25519 signature verification, chain hash verification, Merkle inclusion proof verification, input commitment check, and optional STARK proof verification. Public endpoint, no authentication required.
